entities.rationale: Moral intelligibility is the capacity or internal ground by which moral obligations become comprehensible to agents — an internally grounded enabling disposition inhering in bearers (agents or relational fields), aptly a subclass of Normativity (itself a Disposition under BFO_0000016).

entities.label: ObligationAsGrammar
entities.rationale: The utterance characterizes Obligation not as a volitional limit (a constraint on will) but as a structuring grammar — an internally grounded disposition that constitutes the framework of moral meaning. This is a refinement of ObligationStructure emphasizing its generative, grammar-like character rather than its constraining function.

relations.rationale: ObligationAsGrammar is a more specific kind of ObligationStructure — one characterized by its constitutive, meaning-structuring role rather than its constraining force.

The grammar-of-obligation reading implies that obligation is itself the ground of moral intelligibility; modeling this as a subclass intersection captures the claim that ObligationAsGrammar realizes MoralIntelligibility.

Reinforces that NormativeConstraint (will-limiting reading) and ObligationAsGrammar are co-hyponyms of ObligationStructure, making explicit that the utterance distinguishes the grammar-reading from the constraint-reading.

open_questions: Should ObligationAsGrammar be disjoint with NormativeConstraint to formally encode the claim that the grammar reading excludes the will-limiting reading, or are they merely non-identical (compatible in some bearers)?

Does 'grammar of moral intelligibility' imply a generically dependent continuant (a pattern or structure that could be instantiated across multiple bearers, like a language grammar), rather than a disposition? If so, should ObligationAsGrammar be reclassified under BFO_0000031 (Generically Dependent Continuant)?

Is 'MoralIntelligibility' best understood as a disposition inhering in agents, or as a quality (BFO_0000019) of the relational or normative field? The answer affects whether it should be under Normativity (Disposition) or minted as a Quality subclass.

Should the existing 'Obligation' class be broadened or annotated to note that its primary characterization is as grammar/structuring principle rather than constraint, or should ObligationAsGrammar eventually replace or refine it?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes a substantive philosophical claim: Obligation is not primarily a constraint on will (a limiting, externally-imposed force) but rather a 'grammar of moral intelligibility' — a structuring, constitutive principle that makes moral life coherent and meaningful. In BFO terms, this suggests two new classes. First, MoralIntelligibility as a subclass of Normativity (BFO_0000016 Disposition) captures the capacity or ground by which moral action and reasoning become interpretable. Second, ObligationAsGrammar as a subclass of ObligationStructure captures the constitutive, meaning-structuring role of obligation. A relation links ObligationAsGrammar as a subclass of MoralIntelligibility, encoding the claim that this kind of obligation grounds intelligibility. The existing NormativeConstraint class is explicitly preserved and contrasted as the will-limiting alternative. No individuals are asserted. SituatednessInObligation (BFO_0000019 Quality, subclass of ObligationStructure and Selfhood) captures the qualitative state of the self as already-placed-within-obligation — the phenomenological 'finding oneself' that the utterance foregrounds. entities.label: Freedom
entities.rationale: Freedom, understood as a capacity or condition of agents for self-determination, is internally grounded in the bearer (a conscious being or agent) and is thus best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016). It is a kind of realizable entity that can be exercised or constrained in processes.

entities.label: CoConstitutiveRelation
entities.rationale: The claim that freedom and obligation are co-constitutive asserts a structural interdependence — each requires and partly constitutes the other. This is best captured as a class representing a mutual constitution relation between two disposition classes. Typed under Disposition (BFO_0000016) as it expresses a grounded structural tendency or condition rather than a quality or process.

relations.rationale: Freedom is a subclass of Disposition, grounding the capacity for self-determination in an agent bearer.

Co-constitution with Obligation means Freedom is structurally intertwined with ObligationStructure — it is a disposition that is co-defined by obligation. Asserting Freedom as a subclass of ObligationStructure captures that freedom cannot be understood apart from the obligation structure it co-constitutes. NOTE: this is open to challenge; see open_questions.
Obligation participates in the co-constitutive relation with Freedom.
Freedom participates symmetrically in the co-constitutive relation with Obligation.

Should Freedom be modeled as a subclass of ObligationStructure (implying it is a kind of obligation structure), or should the relation be expressed differently — e.g., via an OWL equivalence or mutual dependency axiom? The subclass relation may be too strong.

Is the co-constitutive claim meant normatively (ethical/philosophical thesis) or descriptively (ontological interdependence)? This affects whether it should be an axiom in the ontology or a comment/annotation.
Should CoConstitutiveRelation be a class (a type of structural condition) or a named OWL object property linking Freedom and Obligation instances?

Ontologically, this requires (1) introducing Freedom as a new class, best typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) since it is an internally grounded capacity of agents; and (2) representing the co-constitutive relationship. The co-constitution is modeled via a new class CoConstitutiveRelation (also a Disposition/structural condition) that both Freedom and Obligation are typed under, capturing their mutual structural interdependence. However, making Freedom a subclass of ObligationStructure is contestable and flagged as an open question. The relation between them might ultimately be better expressed as a symmetric OWL object property or mutual dependency axiom rather than a shared superclass, but that requires non-BFO extensions. proposal.utterance: Obligation defines the ethical topography; freedom is the capacity to move within that terrain.

entities.label: EthicalTopography
entities.rationale: The 'ethical topography' is a structured quality of the normative field defined by obligations — a measurable (in principle) relational property of the moral landscape. Typing as Quality under Normativity captures that it is a specifically dependent continuant inhering in agents-in-relation.

entities.label: AgentiveFreedom
entities.rationale: Freedom as 'capacity to move within the terrain' is an internally grounded disposition of an agent — the disposition to act within an obligation-structured normative field. Typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) and placed under ModeOfParticipation because it expresses how an agent can engage within the ethically structured space.

relations.rationale: EthicalTopography is a species of Normativity — it is the structured normative quality constituted by the distribution of obligations.
Freedom is the mode in which an agent participates within the obligatory terrain — it is the dispositional capacity for action within that structured field.

The utterance asserts that Obligation defines the ethical topography; thus ObligationStructure is a subclass of (or at minimum a definer of) EthicalTopography. This partial subsumption captures that the topography is constituted by the obligation structure.
Freedom as disposition is realized in social processes — the acts of moving within the ethical terrain are social/agentive processes.

open_questions: Should EthicalTopography be a Quality (a static property of the normative field) or a Disposition (a structured capacity of the relational field to constrain)? The metaphor 'topography' suggests a quality, but its defining role could support disposition.

Is AgentiveFreedom meant to be freedom within an already-given obligatory structure (compatibilist sense), or should it contrast with obligation as a separate normative pole? This affects whether it should be coordinated with or subordinate to ObligationStructure.

Should ObligationStructure be strictly a subclass of EthicalTopography, or should the relation be modeled as a 'constitutes' or 'defines' relation (which BFO does not have natively but could be approximated with a custom property)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts two philosophical claims: (1) Obligation structures the ethical field as a kind of 'topography' — a quality of the normative landscape that specifies where agents stand relative to one another; and (2) Freedom is a capacity — specifically a disposition — to act within that structured terrain. I mint EthicalTopography as a Quality-level class under Normativity (capturing the idea that obligation produces a measurable normative field) and AgentiveFreedom as a Disposition under ModeOfParticipation (capturing freedom as an internally grounded capacity for agentive movement within obligation-defined space). The relation between ObligationStructure and EthicalTopography is modeled as subsumption with an open question about whether a richer 'constitutes' predicate is warranted. No individuals are asserted. The metaphysical imagery is conservative and BFO-consistent: the terrain is a quality inhering in relational contexts; the freedom is a disposition realized in processes.

proposal.utterance: A self that denies its entanglement is not sovereign and is cut off from conditions making selfhood possible.

entities.label: EntanglementDenial
entities.rationale: A disposition (internally grounded realizable) of a self to deny its relational entanglement; it is a mode of Selfhood because it characterizes the self's orientation toward its own relational constitution.

entities.label: SelfhoodConditionDeprivation
entities.rationale: A disposition-like state in which the conditions making selfhood possible are blocked or unavailable to a self; the utterance asserts that denial of entanglement produces this state. Typed as a subclass of Selfhood (a disposition) because it describes a deficient mode of selfhood.

entities.label: FalseSovereignty
entities.rationale: The illusory sense of self-sufficiency or sovereignty that accompanies EntanglementDenial; the utterance distinguishes this from genuine sovereignty, so it warrants a distinct class as a pathological Selfhood disposition.

entities.label: SelfhoodPossibilityCondition
entities.rationale: The conditions that make selfhood possible — parallel to ExperiencePossibilityCondition already in the ontology. These are internally-grounded enabling dispositions. Typed under ObligationGeneratingCondition because the existing pattern treats relational enabling conditions as such.

entities.label: RelationalEntanglement
entities.rationale: The state of being constitutively enmeshed in relations with others; a sub-kind of PrimordialRelationality. The utterance treats this as an ontological fact that a self can deny but cannot escape.

relations.rationale: EntanglementDenial is a mode/disposition of Selfhood — a particular orientation a self can bear.
FalseSovereignty is the specific character of the self that results from EntanglementDenial; it is a sub-type of that denial disposition.
SelfhoodConditionDeprivation is a deficient mode of Selfhood — the state of being cut off from conditions making selfhood possible.

The utterance asserts that EntanglementDenial entails SelfhoodConditionDeprivation — a self that denies entanglement is thereby cut off from conditions of selfhood, so EntanglementDenial is a subtype of SelfhoodConditionDeprivation.
RelationalEntanglement is one of the conditions that makes selfhood possible; denying it therefore deprives the self of a SelfhoodPossibilityCondition.
Conditions making selfhood possible are also conditions generating obligations — consistent with the existing pattern of ExperiencePossibilityCondition and PresenceOfOther.
RelationalEntanglement is a sub-kind of PrimordialRelationality already in the ontology.

open_questions: Should 'sovereignty' be modeled as a distinct Role (BFO_0000023) that a self can bear or fail to bear, rather than as a Disposition sub-type of Selfhood? The utterance may imply a normative status rather than an intrinsic property.

Should SelfhoodConditionDeprivation be typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) — a measurable state of lack — rather than a Disposition? Deprivation of conditions might be better understood as a quality of the self rather than a disposition.
Does 'entanglement' refer specifically to RelationalConstitution already in the ontology, or is RelationalEntanglement a genuinely new class that should be distinguished from it?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes three interlocking ontological claims: (1) a self can bear a disposition to deny its relational entanglement (EntanglementDenial); (2) such denial results in a state of being cut off from the conditions making selfhood possible (SelfhoodConditionDeprivation); and (3) the denial produces only a false, not genuine, sovereignty (FalseSovereignty). These claims presuppose that relational entanglement (RelationalEntanglement, a sub-kind of PrimordialRelationality already in the ontology) and its associated enabling conditions (SelfhoodPossibilityCondition, parallel to ExperiencePossibilityCondition) are real ontological structures. All new classes are typed as BFO Dispositions (BFO_0000016) because they are internally grounded realizable entities inhering in conscious beings/selves, and are placed under existing parents in the working ontology to maintain consistency. FalseSovereignty is modeled as a sub-type of EntanglementDenial because the utterance treats it as the specific character — not a separate cause — of the denying self. The relation chain EntanglementDenial ⊑ SelfhoodConditionDeprivation captures the causal/constitutive claim that denial just is the state of being deprived of selfhood conditions.

entities.rationale: The capacity to choose is an internally grounded potential inhering in an agent — a disposition in BFO terms. It is not externally conferred (which would make it a role) but is a real potential of the bearer.

entities.label: CapacityToPromise
entities.rationale: The capacity to promise is likewise a disposition inhering in an agent, grounded in its nature. Promising is a performative act enabled by this disposition.

entities.label: EthicalRelationNetwork
entities.rationale: A network of ethical relations is a structured normative disposition-complex that inheres in a collective of agents. It is normative in character (subclass of existing Normativity), and its BFO type is Disposition (BFO_0000016) since it is an internally grounded, bearer-specific structure. It is the condition within which capacities to choose and promise are formed.

entities.label: FormationWithinEthicalRelation
entities.rationale: Being 'formed within' a network of ethical relations is a developmental social process — a SocialProcess — through which the capacities to choose and promise become realized. This is an occurrent through which the dispositions are constituted.

CapacityToPromise is a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016).

FormationWithinEthicalRelation is a subclass of SocialProcess (BFO_0000015), the occurrent through which agents are constituted within ethical networks.

The CapacityToChoose (disposition) is realized in FormationWithinEthicalRelation — the process of being formed within an ethical relation network is the occasion through which this capacity comes to be actualized.
Similarly, CapacityToPromise is realized in FormationWithinEthicalRelation.
The formation process has the EthicalRelationNetwork as a participant — it is the normative structure within which formation occurs.

open_questions: Should CapacityToChoose and CapacityToPromise be modeled as subclasses of ModeOfParticipation or MaterialGrounding rather than bare Disposition, given the existing class hierarchy relating dispositions to agency?

Should EthicalRelationNetwork be modeled as a Site (BFO_0000029) — an intersubjective space — rather than a Disposition, given that it is a context/milieu rather than a bearer-specific potential? Compare with IntersubjectiveWorld already in the ontology.

The 'network of ethical relations' is modeled as EthicalRelationNetwork, a subclass of the existing Normativity class, itself a Disposition-complex. entities.label: Responsiveness
entities.rationale: Responsiveness is an internally grounded capacity of an agent to respond to the presence and claims of others; it fits as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) since it is a tendency or capacity inhering in a bearer.

entities.label: EthicalSpace
entities.rationale: Ethical space is the normatively structured relational milieu within which the self is constituted. It extends IntersubjectiveWorld (already a subclass of BFO Site) by adding normative/ethical character.

entities.label: SelfCrystallization
entities.rationale: The 'crystallization' of the self from directedness, dependency and responsiveness is a process—a forming or constitution of selfhood—that unfolds in time and in ethical space. It is a subtype of SocialProcess.

relations.rationale: EthicalSpace is a more specific kind of IntersubjectiveWorld, adding normative-ethical character to the intersubjective milieu.

EthicalSpace is also characterized by EthicalTopography; however, since BFO prohibits a single individual from being both a Site and a Disposition, this relation is flagged as potentially problematic and left for human review.
The SelfCrystallization process realizes Selfhood (a Disposition/realizable entity inhering in an agent), consistent with BFO's 'realizes' relation.
Responsiveness is a form of relational directedness—an orientation toward and capacity to answer the claims of others.
SelfCrystallization is a kind of SubjectConstitution (an ObligationProductionProcess), since forming a self from relational elements also produces a moral subject bearing obligations.
Directedness (existing class, RelationalDirectedness subtype) is a constituent input to the SelfCrystallization process; modeled as part-of the process.
DependencyExposure (which captures dependency/vulnerability) is a constituent of the SelfCrystallization process.
Responsiveness is the third constitutive element of SelfCrystallization alongside directedness and dependency.

open_questions: EthicalSpace is proposed as a subclass of both IntersubjectiveWorld (a BFO Site, hence a continuant/immaterial entity) and EthicalTopography (a Normativity subtype, hence a Disposition/SDC). BFO prohibits an entity from being both an independent continuant and a specifically dependent continuant. Should EthicalSpace be modeled only as a Site (with EthicalTopography as a quality/disposition that inheres in or is associated with it), rather than inheriting from both?

The utterance uses 'crystallization' metaphorically. Should SelfCrystallization be a Process (something that happens) or a ProcessProfile? And should its output—the crystallized self—be represented as an individual Selfhood instance that is the result of that process?
Is 'Responsiveness' already implicitly captured by existing classes such as Mutuality or RelationalDirectedness, or is it sufficiently distinct to warrant a new class?
Should 'ethical space' be treated as a type token (a class of sites) or as a singular individual representing a universal normative milieu?

I introduce Responsiveness as a new Disposition (BFO_0000016) that is a subtype of RelationalDirectedness, since it is an internally grounded capacity to answer to others. I introduce EthicalSpace as a Site (BFO_0000029), extending IntersubjectiveWorld, to represent the normatively structured relational milieu. I introduce SelfCrystallization as a SocialProcess (BFO_0000015) that realizes Selfhood and is also a SubjectConstitution; the three elements are modeled as parts of this process. proposal.utterance: Autonomy of the liberal individual is an outcome of ethical formation, not its precondition.

entities.label: Autonomy
entities.rationale: Autonomy is an internally grounded capacity of an agent — a disposition to self-govern. It is not a quality (not measurable on a simple scale) but a realizable capacity, best typed as Disposition (BFO_0000016) under the realizable entity hierarchy.

entities.label: LiberalIndividual
entities.rationale: The 'liberal individual' is a socio-philosophical kind of person — a subclass of Person defined by the political/philosophical tradition of liberal individualism. It is a material entity (a kind of person with a body and continuant identity).

entities.label: EthicalFormation
entities.rationale: Ethical formation is the process through which moral selfhood, normativity, and autonomy are constituted in a person through relational and social engagement. As a happening unfolding in time, it is a Process (BFO_0000015), and it fits naturally as a SocialProcess subtype in the existing ontology.

entities.label: EthicalFormationOutcome
entities.rationale: This class captures the status of Autonomy as a realizable entity that results from (is an outcome of) EthicalFormation. It functions as a superclass or grouping type for dispositions that are produced by ethical formation processes, distinguishing outcome-dispositions from precondition-dispositions.

relations.rationale: The utterance asserts that autonomy is an outcome of ethical formation; typing Autonomy as a subclass of EthicalFormationOutcome captures this claim structurally.
Autonomy as a capacity of a LiberalIndividual is also a mode of participation in social and ethical processes — linking it to the existing ModeOfParticipation disposition hierarchy.
Ethical formation is a social process; it unfolds through intersubjective relational encounters, consistent with the existing SocialProcess class.

EthicalFormation (a process) realizes Autonomy (a disposition) in the bearer — capturing the claim that autonomy is produced by, not prior to, the ethical formation process. BFO_0000055 (realizes) connects process to realizable.
Ethical formation is a kind of obligation-grounding process in this ontology — it produces the normative substrate (including autonomy) through which obligation and moral selfhood emerge.
The liberal individual is a conscious being (a subtype of Person) capable of bearing autonomy as a disposition formed through ethical processes.

open_questions: Should 'Autonomy' be further typed as a subclass of 'Selfhood' (already in the ontology) since it concerns self-governance and identity, or should it remain a sibling class under Disposition/ModeOfParticipation?

Is 'LiberalIndividual' intended as a political-philosophical kind (e.g., Lockean/Kantian tradition), or more broadly as any self-governing agent? This affects whether it should be a subclass of MoralSelf rather than Person directly.
Should 'EthicalFormation' be related to 'SubjectConstitution' (already in the ontology as an ObligationProductionProcess)? They appear to overlap significantly.

The claim implies that autonomy cannot be a precondition of ethical formation — should we add an explicit disjointness or priority axiom, or is the subClassOf EthicalFormationOutcome sufficient to capture this?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes a substantive philosophical claim: autonomy — traditionally posited as a foundational attribute of the liberal individual — is recast here as an emergent outcome of ethical formation rather than its presupposition. This commits us ontologically to (1) Autonomy as a disposition class (BFO_0000016) whose realization depends on an antecedent process; (2) EthicalFormation as a social process (BFO_0000015) that realizes autonomy via BFO_0000055; (3) LiberalIndividual as a subclass of ConsciousBeing/Person — the bearer-type of such autonomy; and (4) EthicalFormationOutcome as a grouping class for dispositions produced by ethical formation, explicitly distinguishing outcome-dispositions from precondition-dispositions. The key ontological move is placing Autonomy downstream of EthicalFormation through the realizes relation, which formally encodes the claim that formation precedes and produces autonomy rather than presupposing it. Connections to existing classes ObligationGrounding and SubjectConstitution are proposed given strong conceptual overlap.

entities.label: SelfCrystallization
entities.rationale: The metaphor of 'crystallization' describes the self as the outcome of a process — an unfolding in time through which selfhood takes shape under pressures. Typing as a SocialProcess (subtype of BFO Process) captures the relational and temporal dimension of this formation.

entities.label: EthicalPressure
entities.rationale: Ethical pressures are internally grounded dispositions of the relational/ethical field that shape the process of self-formation. They are not qualities (not straightforwardly measurable) but dispositional tendencies that can be realized in processes. Subclassing EthicalTopography captures the normative topological metaphor already present in the ontology.

entities.label: SovereignSelfhood
entities.rationale: The utterance explicitly contrasts the crystallized self with a 'sovereign legislator' model of selfhood. Capturing this as a distinct subclass of Selfhood allows the ontology to represent and contrast two models of self-constitution — the sovereign (autonomy-first) vs. the relational-crystallization view. Typed as Disposition because sovereign selfhood is a capacity/tendency attributed to a bearer.

relations.rationale: SelfCrystallization (as a process) realizes Selfhood (a realizable disposition): the self-as-crystallization is the outcome of this process realizing or instantiating selfhood in the agent.

Ethical pressures are a kind of obligation-generating condition: they are the relational-normative forces that both shape selfhood and generate the conditions for moral obligation, consistent with the existing ObligationGeneratingCondition hierarchy.
SelfCrystallization is a species of SubjectConstitution — the process by which a subject (self) is constituted — here specifically via ethical pressures rather than sovereign self-legislation.

SovereignSelfhood is a subtype of Selfhood representing the contrasted (rejected) model of self as autonomous legislator, enabling the ontology to formally represent the conceptual contrast the utterance asserts.

open_questions: Should SelfCrystallization be modeled purely as a process (BFO_0000015) or also give rise to a quality or role that persists in the agent after the process completes? The utterance implies a stable outcome ('crystallization'), which might warrant a companion continuant (e.g., a CrystallizedSelf quality).

Is EthicalPressure intended to be an external relational force (more like a quality of the intersubjective field) or an internal disposition of the agent? This affects whether it should inhere in the IntersubjectiveWorld (site/field) or in the individual agent.

Should SovereignSelfhood be retained as a contrastive/negative concept in this ontology, or is it merely rhetorical contrast? If the ontology is meant to model only the author's positive commitments, it may be omitted.
Does 'ethical pressure' overlap substantially with the existing EthicalTopography or NormativeConstraint classes, potentially warranting subsumption rather than a new class?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes three substantive ontological commitments: (1) selfhood is constituted through a process ('crystallization') rather than being a pre-given sovereign capacity; (2) the shaping forces of this process are specifically ethical in character ('ethical pressures'); and (3) the alternative model — the 'sovereign legislator' self — is implicitly rejected. I represent (1) as a new class SelfCrystallization, a subtype of both SocialProcess and SubjectConstitution, which realizes the existing Selfhood disposition. I represent (2) as EthicalPressure, a disposition subclassing EthicalTopography and ObligationGeneratingCondition, since these pressures are the relational-normative conditions that drive self-formation and simultaneously generate obligation. I represent (3) as SovereignSelfhood, a contrastive subtype of Selfhood, allowing the ontology to formally encode the conceptual opposition the utterance asserts. No individuals are introduced; all entities are classes consistent with BFO typing. Several open questions remain about the exact direction of the inheres-in relation for EthicalPressure and whether SovereignSelfhood should be retained as a purely contrastive concept.

It is externally grounded (characteristic of BFO Role), contingent on historical and institutional context, not an intrinsic or necessary property of persons. SubjectConstitution is an existing parent class that covers processes/structures through which subjects are constituted; however, since the liberal subject is better typed as the role that emerges from such constitution, we type it as a Role (BFO_0000023) and relate it to SubjectConstitution via context.

Generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031) captures information-like, pattern-like constructs that are not tied to a single bearer. The liberal subject as a normative schema qualifies as a GDC.

A social artifact is a generically dependent continuant: a normative or conceptual pattern realized across social contexts, not bound to a single physical bearer.

open_questions: Should LiberalSubject be modeled as a Role (BFO_0000023, borne by individual persons) or as a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031, a normative schema that is transmitted culturally)? The utterance treats it as a constructed artifact (suggesting GDC), but in contexts where a specific person instantiates this subject-position, Role is more precise. The two models may each be needed for different purposes.

The alignment aspect (capacity, context, response) is modeled through structural relations below.

entities.label: Capacity
entities.rationale: Capacity is an internally grounded ability or potential of an agent; this fits BFO Disposition as it is borne by the agent and grounds possible processes.

entities.label: AgentiveContext

entities.label: Response
entities.rationale: Response as a component of agency is an occurrent — a doing or reactive process by an agent. Modeling it as a Process (BFO_0000015) is appropriate.

entities.label: AgencyAlignment
entities.rationale: The 'alignment' of capacity, context, and response is itself a process — the coming-together of these three components that constitutes agency as achievement. Subclassing RelationalAchievement ties it to the existing social-process framework.

proposal.utterance: Rights are ethical outputs and secondary formations, not foundations of ethics.

entities.label: Right
entities.rationale: Rights are normative statuses that inhere in bearers and are realizable in social processes. Typing them as a subclass of ObligationStructure (which is already a Disposition subclass) captures that they are internally grounded, dependent on the social-relational order, and structurally downstream of ethical foundations. This is consistent with the claim that rights are 'secondary formations' rather than foundations.

entities.label: EthicalFoundation
entities.rationale: The utterance contrasts rights (secondary, derivative) against ethics' foundations. EthicalFoundation as a subclass of Normativity captures the primary normative ground from which rights emerge. Typed as Disposition because it is an internally grounded capacity of the normative order that is realized in moral practice.

entities.label: EthicalOutput
entities.rationale: The utterance explicitly characterizes rights as 'ethical outputs'. EthicalOutput as a class under Normativity names the derivative, resultant normative formations that arise from more fundamental ethical conditions. Rights will be asserted as a subclass of EthicalOutput.

entities.label: SecondaryFormation
entities.rationale: The utterance also characterizes rights as 'secondary formations', implying a structural derivativeness. SecondaryFormation names the class of normative entities that are constituted by or derived from more foundational normative conditions, rather than being themselves foundational.

relations.rationale: Rights are asserted to be ethical outputs per the utterance.
Rights are asserted to be secondary formations per the utterance.
Ethical outputs are derived from ethical foundations; they presuppose and emerge from them but are not identical to them. This encodes the asymmetry the utterance asserts.
Secondary formations presuppose primary foundations; the sub-class relation encodes that EthicalFoundation is the more general, prior category from which SecondaryFormation is distinguished.
Rights are part of the obligation-bearing normative structure already present in the ontology; they are downstream normative artifacts rather than generators of obligation.

proposal.utterance: All selves are dependent on infrastructure, education, health systems, and often on care.

entities.label: StructuralDependency
entities.rationale: Selves depend on external structures (infrastructure, education, health, care). This structural dependency is an internally-grounded disposition of the self — a mode of being that is materially grounded. Subclass of MaterialGrounding, which already sits under BFO Disposition.

entities.label: Infrastructure
entities.rationale: Infrastructure (roads, utilities, built systems) is a material entity with mass and spatial extent. It is the physical/systemic substrate on which selves depend.

entities.label: EducationSystem
entities.rationale: An education system is a complex material entity (institutions, buildings, persons, documents) through which educational processes are realized. It is also a site of social processes, but primarily typed as material entity due to its physical instantiation.

entities.label: HealthSystem
entities.rationale: A health system is a complex material entity (hospitals, clinics, practitioners, equipment) enabling care processes. Typed analogously to EducationSystem.

entities.label: CareRelation
entities.rationale: Care (as invoked here) is a social process in which one agent attends to the needs of another, realizing obligations and vulnerability. It is a SocialProcess and also a site of recognition and ethical interdependence.

entities.label: SocialDependency
entities.rationale: Dependency on education, health systems, and care is a socially-mediated subtype of structural dependency — the disposition of a self to require ongoing social and institutional support for its constitution and functioning.

relations.rationale: Structural dependency is a mode of material grounding: it is internally grounded in the self's constitution by material and social infrastructures.
Dependency on social institutions (education, health, care) is a specific form of structural dependency.

Structural dependency is a form of vulnerability: the self's openness to harm or flourishing depending on whether supporting structures are present or absent. Vulnerability is already in the ontology as a subclass of RelationalDirectedness and DependencyExposure.
Care is a social process.
Care processes realize ethical interdependence — the mutual obligations and dependencies between selves that care makes manifest.
Care is an obligation-generating condition: the presence and exercise of care generates duties of response, reciprocity, or non-abandonment.

entities.rationale: Integrity-of-relation is a measurable property (quality) of a relational structure; it is the condition the relation must maintain to persist in a normatively adequate way. It inheres in the relational bearer and is a sub-kind of Relationality.

entities.label: GoodAsRelationalRequirement
entities.rationale: The good, on this account, is not a free-standing object but an internally grounded disposition of agents-in-relation: the disposition to act in ways required for the relation's integrity. It is a sub-kind of Normativity (itself a disposition class in this ontology).

entities.label: RelationalSustenance
entities.rationale: Sustaining a relation with integrity is an occurrent process: the ongoing activity by which agents maintain the relational bond over time. It is a sub-kind of SocialProcess.

entities.label: RelationalJustification
entities.rationale: The claim that the good is 'justified because relation requires it' introduces a justificatory structure grounded in relational obligation. This is a disposition (internally grounded normative capacity) belonging to the obligation structure already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: The good-as-relational-requirement is a species of normativity: a normatively loaded disposition grounded in relational demands.
Justification that derives from relational requirements is a sub-type of obligation structure, since it confers normative warrant on action via relational necessity.
Integrity of relation is a specific quality that qualifies instances of Relationality, characterising them as normatively intact.
Sustaining a relation is a social process unfolding over time.
The disposition toward the good (GoodAsRelationalRequirement) is realized in the process of sustaining the relation with integrity (RelationalSustenance).
The justificatory force of relational requirement is also realized in the process of sustaining the relation, since it is that process that the justification is oriented toward.
Explicit BFO typing: IntegrityOfRelation is a Quality (BFO_0000019).

open_questions: Is 'the good' here intended as a universal moral good (Platonic/objectivist reading) or strictly as an agent-relative, relational good? This affects whether GoodAsRelationalRequirement should be a disposition (internally grounded) or a role (externally conferred).

Should 'integrity' here be typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in a relational structure, or as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) of the agents involved? The current proposal treats it as a quality of the relation itself.

Is 'sustained' here a synchronic (at-a-time) or diachronic (over-time) notion? If diachronic, RelationalSustenance as a Process is appropriate; if synchronic, it might be better modeled as a disposition or quality.

Does 'justified' introduce an epistemic operator (the good is epistemically warranted) or a normative one (the good is obligatory)? This affects whether RelationalJustification should link to an epistemic or deontic sub-structure.
Is the claim meant to be a foundational axiom (the good is constituted by relational requirements) or a contingent one (in typical cases, the good tracks what relations require)?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes a normative-metaphysical claim: that what counts as 'the good' is justified by what sustaining a relation with integrity requires. This introduces at least four new ontological commitments: (1) IntegrityOfRelation as a Quality of relational structures, characterising them as normatively intact; (2) GoodAsRelationalRequirement as a Disposition sub-typing Normativity, since the good is here an internally grounded readiness to act as the relation demands; (3) RelationalSustenance as a SocialProcess, the ongoing activity by which the relation is maintained; and (4) RelationalJustification as a sub-type of ObligationStructure capturing the derived normative warrant. The key structural claim—that the good is realised in the process of relational sustenance—is captured by BFO_0000054 (realized in) links from both GoodAsRelationalRequirement and RelationalJustification to RelationalSustenance. Several open questions remain about the precise modality (epistemic vs. deontic justification), the agent-relative vs. universal scope of 'the good', and whether integrity is better typed as a quality or a disposition.

proposal.utterance: The moral force exists because the structure would collapse without it, like tension in geometry.

entities.label: MoralForce
entities.rationale: Moral force is an internally grounded capacity of a structure to sustain or compel normative coherence; it is disposition-like (BFO_0000016) and falls under ObligationStructure since it is what gives that structure its binding character.

entities.label: StructuralNecessity
entities.rationale: The claim that the structure would collapse without moral force posits a structural necessity — an internally grounded disposition of the relational structure to require certain conditions for its own coherence. This is analogous to geometric tension: a disposition inhering in the structure itself.

entities.label: GeometricAnalogy
entities.rationale: The tension-in-geometry analogy is a representational or conceptual pattern (an information artifact pattern) invoked to explain structural necessity; it is a generically dependent continuant — an abstract explanatory structure that can be instantiated in multiple descriptions.

relations.rationale: Moral force is a species of obligation structure: it is the active, dispositional dimension that gives the obligation structure its normative grip.
Structural necessity is a subspecies of structural dependency: the specific mode of dependency in which the whole collapses if a constitutive element is absent.
Moral force is also a species of normativity, since it is a normatively loaded disposition that prescribes and constrains behavior within the relational structure.
The collapse-without-it claim instantiates constitutive role dependency: moral force plays a constitutive role such that its absence dissolves the structure.

open_questions: Is 'moral force' best understood as a disposition of the relational structure as a whole (inhering in the structure), or as a disposition of individual agents participating in the structure? This affects whether MoralForce should bear toward IntersubjectiveWorld/ObligationStructure or toward ConsciousBeing/MoralSelf.

Should 'structural collapse' be modeled as a process (the breakdown of the relational structure) or as the absence of a quality? If it is a process, we could mint a class CollapseProcess under SocialProcess.

Is the geometric tension analogy meant to do ontological work (i.e., tension IS a kind of structural necessity) or is it purely illustrative? If the former, we might want a TensionLikeNecessity subclass.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes two linked ontological claims: (1) moral force exists and is functionally necessary for a structure, and (2) this necessity is analogous to geometric tension. In BFO terms, moral force is most naturally a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — an internally grounded, realizable entity inhering in the relational or normative structure — modeled as a subclass of ObligationStructure and Normativity. The collapse-without-it logic expresses a StructuralNecessity, a subspecies of StructuralDependency and ConstitutiveRoleDependency already in the ontology, capturing the idea that certain elements are constitutively required for the structure's coherence. The geometric analogy is modeled conservatively as a GeometricAnalogy generically dependent continuant — an explanatory pattern — rather than importing geometric ontology directly. No individuals are asserted; all additions are classes with subclass relations. Three open questions are flagged concerning the bearer of moral force, whether collapse should be reified as a process, and whether the analogy is meant ontologically or rhetorically.

Placing it under Relationality captures its relational character.

entities.label: NecessaryRelationalProperty
entities.rationale: The utterance refers to 'relational properties' that the moral self requires — these are measurable/discernible attributes that inhere in the moral self and are relational in character. Typed as Quality under BFO, subordinated to Relationality as a working class to mark their relational nature.

entities.label: ConstitutiveDependence
entities.rationale: The analogy to the triangle's geometric constraints introduces the notion that MoralSelf has a constitutive dependence — it cannot exist absent certain properties. This is a disposition that, if unrealized, means the MoralSelf fails to exist as such. Typed under StructuralDependency, which already exists in the ontology.

relations.rationale: ConstitutiveDependence is a species of StructuralDependency — the structural form that makes a thing's identity impossible without certain relational conditions.
The properties in question are relational in nature and inherit from the existing Relationality class.
Relational constraints constitutive of the MoralSelf fall under the Relationality disposition family.

Expresses that every MoralSelf instance bears a ConstitutiveDependence — i.e., it cannot exist without those relational properties being satisfied. This mirrors the triangle analogy: the triangle-type cannot be instantiated absent its constitutive geometric constraints.
Relational constraints are a species of constitutive dependence, specifying that the dependency is relational (not merely material or causal).

open_questions: Should ConstitutiveDependence be modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) or as a more abstract relation (e.g., an OWL restriction using existential quantification over NecessaryRelationalProperty)? The disposition reading captures the internal groundedness, but a restriction might be more tractable for reasoning.

The triangle analogy could suggest that absence of these properties makes MoralSelf simply impossible (logical/definitional necessity) rather than merely hard to realize (empirical disposition). Should we encode this as an owl:hasKey or equivalent necessary condition rather than a Disposition?

Is 'NecessaryRelationalProperty' as a Quality class the right move, or would the existing Relationality disposition class (BFO_0000016) suffice to cover what the utterance calls 'relational properties'?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a constitutive dependency thesis: the MoralSelf is like a geometric figure in that certain relational properties are not merely contingently associated with it but are constitutively necessary for its existence. I introduce three new classes. ConstitutiveDependence (under StructuralDependency, typed as Disposition/BFO_0000016) captures the general form of this necessity — a bearer that instantiates it cannot exist without certain conditions obtaining. ConstitutiveRelationalConstraint (under Relationality) is the specifically relational species of such a constraint. NecessaryRelationalProperty (Quality/BFO_0000019, under Relationality) names the properties themselves that must inhere in or be relatable to the MoralSelf. The key relation added is that MoralSelf is subsumed by ConstitutiveDependence, expressing that all instances of MoralSelf bear this dependence structure. No new individuals are introduced; all typing is against existing BFO categories. Several open questions flag whether OWL restrictions rather than new classes are preferable for encoding the logical necessity the triangle analogy implies.

entities.label: ProximityWithRecognitionCapacity
entities.rationale: Being in proximity with capacity for recognition is an internally-grounded condition that, when triggered, generates obligations. It is distinct from individual directedness in being a shared emergent field.

entities.label: ObligationFromFieldOfDirectedness
entities.rationale: The obligation generated by entering a field of directedness is a normative disposition that is realized when two beings with recognition capacity are co-present. proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a structural claim: co-presence plus recognition capacity triggers entry into a normative relational field that generates obligations. Three new classes are proposed. 'ProximityWithRecognitionCapacity' is the trigger condition, typed as a subclass of ObligationGeneratingCondition (BFO_0000016 Disposition) because it is an internally-grounded readiness that, when the right conditions obtain, gives rise to a normative field. entities.rationale: A moral orientation is an internally grounded directedness toward moral engagement — a disposition (BFO_0000016) that characterizes how an agent is oriented toward others. It is not externally defined (so not a Role) but is an intrinsic normative character, fitting under the existing Normativity disposition cluster.

entities.label: MoralObject
entities.rationale: A moral object is an entity insofar as it occupies a socially/externally grounded position as the target or recipient of moral consideration — a Role (BFO_0000023). The utterance explicitly contrasts the 'other as moral orientation' with 'moral object', so the latter must be introduced to allow the distinction to be modeled. Placing it under MeaningBearer (already a Role subclass) captures the idea that the other as moral object is a normatively laden relational role.

entities.label: OtherAsOrientation
entities.rationale: This class captures the specific thesis of the utterance: that the other (as encountered in this ontology) functions as a moral orientation — an intrinsic directedness of the subject toward the other — rather than as an external target. It is a subtype of MoralOrientation and sits within the Disposition hierarchy. It is closely related to RelationalDirectedness but is distinguished as normatively charged rather than merely relational.

relations.rationale: MoralOrientation is a kind of normative disposition, making Normativity the appropriate parent in the working ontology hierarchy.

A moral object is a role-type that a bearer occupies as the target of moral consideration; MeaningBearer (already a Role subclass) is the closest existing parent capturing normatively significant role-occupancy.
OtherAsOrientation is a specific species of MoralOrientation — the case where the other is constituted as a normative directedness rather than an objectified target.

The other-as-orientation is also a form of relational directedness (already in the ontology), making this cross-hierarchy subClassOf assertion appropriate to capture its relational character alongside its normative character.

Being oriented toward the other as a moral orientation carries an intrinsic ethical charge — this subClassOf link to the existing IntrinsicEthicalCharge class captures that the orientation is not merely relational but normatively loaded from within the subject.

open_questions: Should 'MoralOrientation' be treated as a disposition of the subject (agent/person) who encounters the other, or as a quality of the encounter itself? This affects whether it inheres in Person or in a process like Recognition.

Is 'the other' here a specific individual placeholder (e.g., working:TheOther as an individual) or always a class-level construct (AnyOtherPerson)? If the ontology uses phenomenological vocabulary, an abstract individual may be warranted.

Should MoralObject be retained as a contrast class for completeness, or is it explicitly excluded from this ontology (i.e., the ontology asserts that no instance of MoralObject exists)? This would be a closed-world assertion that may be worth flagging.

This distinction maps cleanly onto BFO's contrast between Role (externally grounded, BFO_0000023) and Disposition (internally grounded, BFO_0000016). Cross-hierarchy subClassOf links to RelationalDirectedness and IntrinsicEthicalCharge tie the new classes into existing structure. Several open questions remain about bearer-assignment and whether MoralObject is a genuine contrast class or an excluded kind.

proposal.utterance: Procedural and ideal theories locate normativity in process and rational agreement.

entities.label: ProceduralTheoryOfNormativity
entities.rationale: A procedural theory is an information artifact — a theoretical content that can be instantiated in different texts or minds — locating normativity in process. As a type of theory about normativity, it is a subclass of Normativity only in the sense that it is a generically dependent continuant whose content concerns normativity. However, BFO typing must be precise: theories are GDCs (BFO_0000031). The parent within working ontology is left as Normativity with an open question about whether a dedicated 'TheoryOfNormativity' superclass is needed.

entities.label: IdealTheoryOfNormativity
entities.rationale: An ideal theory locates normativity in rational agreement — again a theoretical content (GDC). Parallel to ProceduralTheoryOfNormativity.

entities.label: RationalAgreement
entities.rationale: Rational agreement is an occurrent social process in which agents reach consensus through reasoning. It is a subclass of SocialProcess (already in the ontology), which is itself a subclass of BFO Process.

entities.label: NormativityInProcess
entities.rationale: The procedural view holds that normative force inheres in and is realized through process rather than in antecedent facts or ideal reason. This is a disposition-like property (realizable entity) that is realized in processes. Subclass of Normativity.

relations.rationale: Procedural theories are generically dependent continuants — theoretical contents.
Ideal theories are generically dependent continuants — theoretical contents.
Procedural theories characteristically locate normative force in process, so instances of this theory class are committed to NormativityInProcess.
Rational agreement is a social process — agents interacting discursively to reach shared conclusions.
NormativityInProcess as a realizable entity is realized in social processes — it is through process that normative force, on the procedural view, becomes actual.

Ideal theories also locate normativity in a process (rational agreement), so they too are committed to NormativityInProcess, though their distinctive mark is that the process must meet idealized rational conditions.

open_questions: Should we introduce a superclass 'TheoryOfNormativity' (BFO_0000031 / GDC) to cleanly gather ProceduralTheoryOfNormativity and IdealTheoryOfNormativity rather than making them direct subclasses of Normativity (which is BFO_0000016)?

The utterance contrasts procedural theories (normativity in process) with ideal theories (normativity in rational agreement). Are these mutually exclusive, or does rational agreement count as a species of process on this view? This affects whether IdealTheoryOfNormativity should be a sibling or subclass of ProceduralTheoryOfNormativity.

Is 'rational agreement' intended as a fully idealized counterfactual process (Habermasian ideal speech situation) or an actual empirical process? The ontological typing differs: a counterfactual ideal might be better typed as a GDC (a model or norm-content) rather than a BFO Process.

Should NormativityInProcess be modeled as a disposition (BFO_0000016) or as a quality (BFO_0000019)? If normative force is a graded or measurable property it might be a quality; if it is a capacity that needs to be triggered/realized it is a disposition.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a meta-theoretical claim: procedural theories place the ground of normativity in process, while ideal theories place it in rational agreement. No individuals are named; these are claims about kinds of normative theories. I mint two new GDC classes (ProceduralTheoryOfNormativity, IdealTheoryOfNormativity) because theories are information content — generically dependent continuants. I also mint RationalAgreement as a SocialProcess subclass (it is an occurrent) and NormativityInProcess as a Normativity subclass (realizable entity / disposition) to capture the philosophical claim that normative force is grounded in process on these views. The relation BFO_0000054 (realized in) connects NormativityInProcess to SocialProcess, expressing that this disposition is actualized through process. I flag several open questions because the procedural/ideal distinction maps ambiguously onto BFO process vs. GDC, and the exact relationship between the two theory types is philosophically contested.

entities.rationale: An ethical structure is an internally grounded, emergent configuration that arises from and is borne by agents in relation. It is not a process itself but a realizable entity — a structured disposition — that is generated when certain relational conditions obtain. Subclassing GenerativeStructure (itself a Disposition) captures the idea that it is a structure with causal-normative potency, not merely a quality.

entities.label: DirectedTowardOther
entities.rationale: Being 'directed toward another' is a specific form of relational directedness — an agent's intentional orientation toward a second agent. This is distinct from AddressedByOther (which is the passive pole) and captures the active directedness that is one condition for the ethical structure's formation. It inheres in the directing agent.

entities.label: CapacityForAddress
entities.rationale: Being 'capable of address' is an intrinsic, internally grounded capacity inhering in the second agent — the disposition to be addressed, to receive and respond to a directed ethical encounter. This grounds the legitimacy of the ethical structure; without this capacity in the other, the structure cannot form. Subclasses ModeOfParticipation since it concerns how an agent can participate in relational encounters.

entities.label: EthicalStructureFormation
entities.rationale: The 'forming' of an ethical structure is itself a process — a relational emergence event — that occurs when the two dispositions (DirectedTowardOther and CapacityForAddress) are co-present and realized. Subclasses RelationalEmergence, as this is precisely the kind of relational genesis described by Butler and similar frameworks already represented in the ontology.

relations.rationale: EthicalStructure is a species of GenerativeStructure: it is a disposition with normative generative power.
Active directedness toward another is a species of RelationalDirectedness.
The capacity to be addressed is a mode of participation in relational-ethical encounters.
The formation of an ethical structure is a relational emergence process.
The EthicalStructureFormation process realizes the EthicalStructure disposition — the structure is the realizable that is brought into realization through this process.
The formation process realizes (or requires the prior realization of) the DirectedTowardOther disposition in the directing agent.
The formation process requires and realizes the CapacityForAddress disposition in the addressed agent.
EthicalStructure is also a normative disposition, warranting cross-typing under Normativity as a broader parent. Modeling as additional subClassOf assertion to capture normative character explicitly.

open_questions: Should EthicalStructure also be typed under ObligationStructure (via ObligationGeneratingCondition) given that the utterance implies obligation-like bindingness when the directed-toward relation obtains?

Is DirectedTowardOther intended to be the active counterpart to the existing AddressedByOther class (passive pole), making them complementary correlates in a dyadic structure? If so, should a formal correlate relation be asserted between them?

Does 'capable of address' mean merely responsive (a cognitive/relational capacity), or does it also entail moral status (vulnerability, face)? The answer affects whether CapacityForAddress should also subclass IntrinsicEthicalCharge.

Is EthicalStructure a type-level universal (a class of dispositions that all such directed encounters instantiate) or should it also have an individual token for specific dyadic encounters? The current proposal treats it as a class.
Should EthicalStructureFormation be constrained by a necessary-participant restriction linking it to exactly two Agents, one bearing DirectedTowardOther and one bearing CapacityForAddress?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a condition of formation: an ethical structure comes into being when one agent is directionally oriented toward another agent who possesses the capacity to be addressed. This involves three distinct ontological commitments: (1) a new class of realizable entity, EthicalStructure, which is an ethically normative generative structure that inheres in or spans the relational configuration of two agents; (2) two dispositional classes — DirectedTowardOther (the active pole, inhering in the first agent) and CapacityForAddress (the passive pole inhering in the second agent) — which together are the enabling conditions for that structure to emerge; and (3) a process class, EthicalStructureFormation, which is the event of that structure coming to be, i.e., a relational emergence. The existing classes AddressedByOther and RelationalDirectedness are reused as parents where appropriate, and the new classes integrate naturally into the existing relational and normative architecture. No individuals are asserted since the utterance is a universal claim about kinds.

proposal.utterance: Recognition is ontological, revealing something about the world.

entities.label: OntologicalDisclosure
entities.rationale: The claim that Recognition is 'ontological' and 'revealing something about the world' posits that Recognition carries a disclosure function directed at reality itself, not merely at intersubjective or normative content. This is best captured as a subtype of ExperientialDisclosure (already a SocialProcess subclass) that specifically grounds its revelatory character in how the world is structured. As a disposition-like capacity of the Recognition process to reveal ontological structure, it fits under BFO_0000016 (Disposition/Realizable). We keep it as a class since the utterance speaks generically of Recognition.

relations.rationale: The utterance asserts that Recognition (as a class of processes already in the ontology) is ontological and world-revealing. Subclassing Recognition under OntologicalDisclosure makes that property inheritable by all instances of Recognition. Alternatively this can be read as Recognition bearing an OntologicalDisclosure disposition, but given OntologicalDisclosure is framed as a character of the kind Recognition, subclassing is the cleaner commitment here.

OntologicalDisclosure is a species of ExperientialDisclosure that is specifically directed at revealing world-structure rather than merely social or intersubjective content, keeping it within the established hierarchy.

open_questions: Does 'ontological' here mean Recognition discloses facts about independently existing entities (realist reading), or that it constitutes the relational being of agents (constitutive reading)? This affects whether OntologicalDisclosure should be typed as a Quality of the world revealed, a Disposition of the recognizing agent, or a character of the Recognition process itself.

Should Recognition's ontological character be modeled as Recognition bearing an OntologicalDisclosure disposition (via RO_0000053) rather than as a subclass relation, given Recognition is already typed as a BFO_0000015 Process?

Is 'revealing something about the world' meant to assert a generically dependent content (like a propositional disclosure, a BFO_0000031) that Recognition produces, which would suggest an output relation rather than a subclass?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes a philosophically substantive claim: Recognition is not merely a social or normative process but is ontological in that it discloses or reveals genuine features of reality. The existing class Recognition is already typed as a Process with parents including InterConsciousEncounter, ObligationGeneratingCondition, RelationalDirectedness, SocialProcess, and BFO_0000015. To honor the new claim without destabilizing existing typing, I introduce OntologicalDisclosure as a new class under ExperientialDisclosure (itself a SocialProcess subtype), representing the revelatory, world-disclosing character that Recognition instances carry. Recognition is then subclassed under OntologicalDisclosure to propagate this property to all instances. This is conservative: it adds one class and one subclass relation, leaves all existing parents intact, and the open questions flag the deeper interpretive ambiguities for the user to resolve before committing.

entities.label: OntologicalDisclosure
entities.rationale: The claim that Recognition 'reveals something about the world' posits an ontological disclosive character — a disposition or capacity of Recognition to disclose features of reality (not merely mental states). Subclassing under Normativity is appropriate because disclosing objective relational facts grounds normative obligations. BFO_0000016 (Disposition) captures that this is an internally grounded, realizable property of the Recognition process.

entities.label: OntologicalCharacter
entities.rationale: The utterance asserts that Recognition has an ontological character — a genuine quality pertaining to it rather than a merely epistemic or psychological feature. As a Quality (BFO_0000019), it is a specifically dependent continuant inhering in the Recognition process or its participant. Placing it under Selfhood links the ontological weight of Recognition to what it reveals about persons and their relational constitution.

relations.rationale: Asserting that Recognition is ontological commits the ontology to Recognition instances bearing the OntologicalDisclosure disposition — i.e., Recognition as a class has a dispositive property of world-disclosure. Using subClassOf encodes that every Recognition event carries this character.

The ontological character of Recognition — that it discloses real features of the world — is the ground of its intrinsic ethical charge. This subClassOf relation captures that every instance of OntologicalCharacter is simultaneously an instance of IntrinsicEthicalCharge, linking the metaphysical and normative aspects.

open_questions: Should OntologicalDisclosure be typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in Recognition instances, or as a Process quality — i.e., a Quality (BFO_0000019) of the Recognition event itself? The two modelings carry different inferential implications.

Does 'reveals something about the world' imply that Recognition generates new social facts (ontological constitution), or that it tracks pre-existing relational facts (ontological discovery)? This distinction may require separate subclasses.

Is the intended contrast 'not just the mind' targeting a purely phenomenological reading of Recognition (Hegel/Honneth) versus a more realist social-ontological one (Searle/Tuomela)? This would affect how OntologicalDisclosure relates to Intentionality already in the ontology.
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes a substantive ontological claim: Recognition is not merely an epistemic or psychological event but one that discloses or constitutes features of reality. First, OntologicalDisclosure (a Disposition subclass of ExperientialDisclosure and Normativity) captures the realizable capacity of Recognition to reveal world-structures. Second, OntologicalCharacter (a Quality subclassing IntrinsicEthicalCharge) encodes the thesis that the ontological weight of Recognition is itself a quality grounding ethical obligations — connecting the metaphysical claim to the normative infrastructure already present. The relation making Recognition a subclass of OntologicalDisclosure ensures every Recognition event inherits this world-disclosing character. No new individuals are minted; all additions are class-level, conservative, and tied to BFO typing.

entities.label: Obligation

proposal.utterance: A lie disrupts mutual intelligibility by introducing dissonance into the structure whose function is sustained recognition.

entities.label: Lie
entities.rationale: A lie is a communicative act—a process that unfolds in time—whose defining feature is intentional falsification directed at another agent. It is a sub-kind of SocialProcess because it occurs between agents in an intersubjective context.

entities.label: MutualIntelligibility
entities.rationale: Mutual intelligibility is the shared capacity of agents to make sense of one another within an intersubjective world. It is a collectively grounded disposition—internally structured but socially expressed—that inheres in a community or dyad of agents. It is closely related to MoralIntelligibility but is broader (covering semantic-pragmatic shared sense-making), so a new subclass of Normativity is warranted.

entities.label: Dissonance
entities.rationale: Dissonance is a quality—a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (here, a relational structure or process) and marks the degree of conflict, incoherence, or misalignment within that structure. It is not a process or a role but a measurable property of the relational configuration.

entities.label: SustainedRecognitionStructure
entities.rationale: The utterance refers to 'the structure whose function is sustained recognition'—a generative relational structure whose proper function is to maintain ongoing Recognition processes between agents. This is a disposition (in BFO: a realizable entity grounded in material/social arrangement) with Recognition as its characteristic realization.

relations.rationale: A lie is a kind of social process; it requires at least two agents and an intersubjective context.
Mutual intelligibility is a normative capacity—a disposition to sustain shared sense-making—grounding it under Normativity alongside MoralIntelligibility and MeaningBearing.
Dissonance is a quality inhering in a relational structure, marking its degree of internal conflict.
The structure whose function is sustained recognition is a generative structure with Recognition as its characteristic realization target.
The SustainedRecognitionStructure is realized in Recognition processes; 'realized in' (BFO_0000054) connects a realizable to the process type in which it is characteristically expressed.

A lie participates in (disrupts) the SustainedRecognitionStructure; using 'participates in' as the closest BFO relation for a process bearing on a structure. Note: strictly BFO 'participates in' links continuants to processes; this relation flags a modeling tension for the open questions.
Mutual intelligibility is the normative-functional character of the SustainedRecognitionStructure; it is the capacity whose disruption by the lie is at stake.

open_questions: 1. 'SocialProcess' is referenced as a parent for Lie and others, but it does not appear in the existing working classes list. Should it be added as a new class (subclass of BFO_0000015) or is there an equivalent already in the ontology under a different label?

2. The relation 'participates in' (RO_0000056) strictly links a continuant to a process in BFO, but here we need to relate a process (Lie) to a structure (SustainedRecognitionStructure, typed as Disposition). Would you prefer a custom 'disrupts' object property, or should we model the interaction differently (e.g., the lie causes Dissonance to inhere in the structure)?

3. Should MutualIntelligibility be modeled as a subclass of SustainedRecognitionStructure, or rather as a quality or disposition that inheres in the community of agents who bear it? The current proposal treats it as a disposition under Normativity and simultaneously as a structural kind, which may require disjointness checking.

4. Is 'Dissonance' better typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) inhering in the SustainedRecognitionStructure, or as a Process (BFO_0000015) that the lie initiates within that structure? The utterance says the lie 'introduces dissonance into the structure', which could support either reading.
5. Should 'Encounter' (parent of InterConsciousEncounter) be added as an explicit class in the ontology, since it is referenced in the existing class hierarchy but not listed among working classes?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes three core ontological claims: (a) there exists a structure whose characteristic function is the ongoing sustaining of Recognition—modeled here as SustainedRecognitionStructure, a Disposition/GenerativeStructure realized in Recognition processes; (b) Mutual Intelligibility is the normative capacity that this structure maintains, typed as a Disposition under Normativity; and (c) a Lie is a Social Process that introduces Dissonance—a Quality—into that structure, thereby disrupting its realization. Four new classes are proposed: Lie (Process/SocialProcess), MutualIntelligibility (Disposition/Normativity), Dissonance (Quality), and SustainedRecognitionStructure (Disposition/GenerativeStructure). The most significant modeling tension is the 'disrupts' relationship: BFO's 'participates in' is designed for continuant-to-process links, so the relation between the Lie process and the SustainedRecognitionStructure disposition is flagged as an open question requiring either a custom property or a remodeling step (e.g., the Lie causes an instance of Dissonance to inhere in the structure). Several parent classes (SocialProcess, Encounter) are referenced in the existing hierarchy but not listed in the context, which also requires clarification before committing.

entities.label: TheGood
entities.rationale: The Good as treated here is a normative orientation or disposition inhering in agents or practices — not a named, possessable, or codifiable object. Modeling it as a subclass of Normativity (itself a BFO Disposition) captures its internally-grounded, non-object character. It is not a material entity, not a generically dependent continuant (it cannot be copied or transmitted as information), and not a site.

entities.rationale: The claim that the good cannot be codified is an assertion about a structural feature of normative phenomena — specifically a resistance to being captured in generically dependent continuants (rules, codes, texts). This is a disposition-like property of TheGood: it resists formal encoding. Placed under Normativity to keep it in the normative cluster.

relations.rationale: TheGood is a kind of normative disposition — it inheres in agents, practices, or relations rather than existing as a discrete possessable object.
Uncodifiability is a normative-structural feature, a disposition of TheGood to resist reduction to any generically dependent continuant (a code, rule, or named concept).

The utterance directly asserts that the good has the property of uncodifiability — every instance of TheGood bears the disposition Uncodifiability. Modeling TheGood as a subclass of Uncodifiability captures that this is a necessary, not contingent, feature.

In BFO terms this means the good is not a material entity (BFO_0000040), not a generically dependent continuant (BFO_0000031, which covers codifiable information), and not an independent continuant generally (BFO_0000004, which covers possessable things). The positive ontological commitment is that the good is normative — it inheres in agents, encounters, or practices rather than standing apart as an object. I therefore propose TheGood as a new class under the existing Normativity cluster (itself typed as BFO Disposition, BFO_0000016), and Uncodifiability as a companion dispositional class capturing the structural resistance to formal encoding. proposal.utterance: We are constituted by relation; relation is not external to the self.

entities.label: ConstitutiveRelationality
entities.rationale: The claim that relation constitutes the self—rather than being external to it—asserts that relationality is an internally grounded, identity-constitutive disposition inhering in the person. It is a subtype of the existing Relationality disposition class, with the specific commitment that this relation is intrinsic (constitutive), not merely extrinsic.

entities.label: InternalRelationalGrounding
entities.rationale: Distinguishes the grounding of self in relation as internal (not external) from cases where relational grounding might be treated as merely contingent or extrinsic. This captures the ontological claim that relation is not external to the self.

relations.rationale: ConstitutiveRelationality is a species of Relationality, specializing it to cases where relational structure is constitutive of (not merely related to) the self.
InternalRelationalGrounding refines RelationalGrounding by asserting that the relational grounding of selfhood is intrinsic, not external—directly encoding the utterance's philosophical claim.

The utterance asserts that relation constitutes the self; modeled as ConstitutiveRelationality being a subclass of Selfhood dispositions—i.e., constitutive relationality is part of what selfhood is, not merely something that happens to self.
InternalRelationalGrounding is the more specific material/structural realization of constitutive relationality, so it is a subclass of ConstitutiveRelationality.

open_questions: Is the claim that *all* selves are constituted by relation (universal/essential), or only that some selves are so constituted (contingent)? This affects whether ConstitutiveRelationality should be modeled as a necessary disposition of Person or as a subtype that only some persons bear.

Should 'constituted by relation' be modeled as a generative process (e.g., RelationalEmergence already in the ontology) rather than or in addition to a disposition? The utterance could be read as asserting both a processual origin and an ongoing structural fact.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a strong metaphysical claim: that relational structure is not merely external to the self but constitutive of it. Ontologically, this is best captured as a disposition (BFO_0000016) that inheres in persons—since dispositions are internally grounded properties of their bearers—specifically a subspecies of Relationality (already in the ontology). Two new classes are proposed: ConstitutiveRelationality (the disposition of being constituted by relation, subtype of both Relationality and Selfhood) and InternalRelationalGrounding (the material-structural basis for that constitution, subtype of RelationalGrounding). The subclass of Selfhood relation encodes the key philosophical move: that constitutive relationality is not external to but definitive of selfhood. No individuals are asserted. Several open questions remain about the scope and modality of the claim.

entities.label: Withdrawal

entities.label: Evasion
entities.rationale: Evasion is the failure-mode contrasted with Recognition: a disposition to avoid the full acknowledgment of another. Typed as Disposition under RelationalDirectedness.

entities.label: Attention
entities.rationale: Attention here denotes the sustained, non-reductive focus of an agent's intentional directedness toward another. It is an internally-grounded capacity, a Disposition under Intentionality.

entities.label: Reduction
entities.rationale: Reduction (as opposed to Attention) is the disposition to diminish or objectify the other, collapsing their full moral presence. Typed as a Disposition under RelationalDirectedness.
