proposal.utterance: Wrongdoing is the unraveling of presence, care, and addressability between persons.

entities.label: Wrongdoing
entities.rationale: Wrongdoing is an occurrent: something that happens, that unfolds in time between persons. It is a social process because it essentially involves inter-personal relations (presence, care, addressability). Modeling it as a subclass of SocialProcess captures both its processual character and its social situatedness.

entities.label: Presence
entities.rationale: Presence here is a relational capacity that an agent bears toward another — a disposition to be manifest, available, and open to an other. It is internally grounded in the bearer (a person), realized in inter-personal encounters. Subclassing under Relationality aligns with the existing pattern for relational dispositions in this ontology.

entities.label: Care
entities.rationale: Care is a normatively loaded disposition: it is a capacity to be concerned with, attentive to, and responsible for an other. It is internally grounded in the bearer and has normative force (it generates obligations and responsiveness). Subclassing under Normativity captures this normative dimension; it could also inherit from Relationality, which is flagged as an open question.

entities.label: Addressability
entities.rationale: Addressability is the disposition of a person to be reachable by, and responsive to, another person's address. It is closely related to AddressedByOther (being addressed) but is the underlying capacity/disposition that makes that possible. Subclassing under RelationalDirectedness fits the existing taxonomy of directedness-related dispositions.

entities.label: RelationalUnraveling
entities.rationale: The utterance characterizes wrongdoing as an 'unraveling' — a processual dissolution or degradation of relational bonds. RelationalUnraveling is the general class of processes in which relational ties (presence, care, addressability) are degraded or severed. Wrongdoing is then a subclass of RelationalUnraveling, adding normative character.

relations.rationale: Wrongdoing is characterized as a specific kind of relational unraveling — the normatively culpable variant. This subsumption relates the general process class to the morally salient subtype.
Relational unraveling is a social process: it involves and affects inter-personal relational structures.
Wrongdoing, as a form of relational unraveling between persons, is a social process — it necessarily involves participants who stand in social and moral relations.
Presence is a relational disposition, situated in the broader class of relational dispositions already in the ontology.
Care is normatively constituted; it generates obligations and is the basis for moral responsiveness.
Addressability is a disposition that grounds directedness toward and from an other; it belongs under the family of RelationalDirectedness dispositions.

A relational unraveling process realizes (or more precisely, degrades/frustrates) the disposition of Presence — it is the processual dissolution of presence between persons. NOTE: BFO_0000055 (realizes) is being used loosely here as 'involves the degradation of'; this relation should be reviewed, as BFO realizes is strictly a positive realization. Flagged in open_questions.
Relational unraveling involves the frustration or dissolution of the disposition of Care. Same caveat as above.
Relational unraveling involves the dissolution of the disposition of Addressability. Same caveat as above.

open_questions: Should Care also subclass Relationality (in addition to or instead of Normativity), since care is both relationally constituted and normatively loaded?

BFO BFO_0000055 (realizes) strictly denotes that a process brings a disposition to its full manifestation. The intended relation here is closer to 'dissolves' or 'frustrates' the disposition. Should we mint a new object property such as working:dissolves or working:frustrates (as a sub-property or inverse of realizes) to accurately capture the unraveling of Presence, Care, and Addressability?
Should Presence also subclass MaterialGrounding or EmbodiedExistence, given that phenomenological presence is typically body-grounded?
Is Wrongdoing intended to be a class of processes (types of wrongdoing) or a universal that applies to any process meeting the unraveling criterion? (The current proposal treats it as a class.)

Should Wrongdoing additionally bear a subclassing relation to a NormativeViolation or ObligationBreach class that does not yet exist in the ontology, to mark its normative character as distinct from mere accidental relational dissolution?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes a substantive philosophical claim: wrongdoing is not merely a rule-violation but an ontological event — a process in which the relational fabric of presence, care, and addressability between persons comes apart. BFO-grounded modeling requires parsing the claim into (a) processes (the unraveling, wrongdoing itself), (b) dispositions (presence, care, and addressability as capacities that inhere in persons and are borne in their relational existence), and (c) the structural relation between the process and those dispositions. Wrongdoing is modeled as a subclass of a newly minted RelationalUnraveling (itself a SocialProcess), and Presence, Care, and Addressability are modeled as disposition classes under the existing Relationality, Normativity, and RelationalDirectedness branches respectively. The principal ontological tension is that BFO's 'realizes' relation is positive (a process brings a disposition to manifestation), whereas the claim here is negative (a process dissolves or frustrates dispositions); a custom 'dissolves' property may be warranted and is flagged for user decision.

proposal.utterance: Being moral involves resisting the unraveling of relational fields and maintaining openness.

entities.label: RelationalFieldResistance
entities.rationale: The capacity to resist the unraveling of relational fields is an internally grounded disposition (BFO_0000016) of an agent or moral subject. It is normative in character and thus best housed under working:Normativity, which already covers internally grounded normative dispositions.

entities.label: RelationalOpenness
entities.rationale: Maintaining openness toward relational fields is a standing disposition of an agent, internally grounded in their relational constitution. It is best typed as a BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) subsumed under working:Relationality, since it characterizes a mode of relational orientation.

entities.label: MoralFieldUnraveling
entities.rationale: The unraveling of relational/moral fields is a process (BFO_0000015) — a temporal happening that can be resisted. It is a sub-process within the broader category of MoralFieldRealization (the enacting or dis-enacting of moral fields in time).

entities.label: MoralConductDisposition
entities.rationale: Being moral, as described here, is a complex disposition to act in certain ways — resisting field unraveling and maintaining openness. This class provides a superclass that integrates RelationalFieldResistance and RelationalOpenness as components of moral conduct.

relations.rationale: Resisting relational field unraveling is one component of the broader disposition to be moral.
Maintaining openness to relational fields is a co-constitutive component of the moral conduct disposition.
The disposition to resist field unraveling is realized in moral field realization processes — it is precisely in such processes that the disposition manifests.
Moral conduct dispositions are normative dispositions and fall under the Normativity hierarchy already established in the ontology.
Unraveling of a moral field is a specific kind of moral field realization process — one with a negative trajectory.

open_questions: Is 'being moral' best understood here as a standing disposition of agents (BFO_0000016), or should it also be partially constituted by a process class (BFO_0000015) representing acts of moral conduct? The current proposal treats it as a disposition realized in processes.
Should 'RelationalOpenness' be typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) — a measurable property of an agent's relational stance — rather than a Disposition? It could be argued either way.

Does 'unraveling of relational fields' refer specifically to working:MoralField instances, or more broadly to any relational field (including non-moral ones)? If broader, MoralFieldUnraveling may need a sibling class RelationalFieldUnraveling under SocialProcess.

Is 'openness' here intentional directedness toward others (suggesting a subclass of RelationalDirectedness) rather than a dispositional property? Should RelationalOpenness be moved under working:RelationalDirectedness?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that moral conduct has two essential components: (1) actively resisting the dissolution of relational/moral fields, and (2) maintaining an open relational orientation toward others. Both are internally grounded features of agents — dispositions in the BFO sense (BFO_0000016). I introduce RelationalFieldResistance and RelationalOpenness as disposition classes under Normativity and Relationality respectively, and a unifying superclass MoralConductDisposition under Normativity. I also introduce MoralFieldUnraveling as a Process (BFO_0000015) — the event-type that moral agents resist — placed under the existing MoralFieldRealization class. The resistance disposition is linked via BFO_0000054 (realized in) to MoralFieldRealization processes. Several open questions remain about whether openness is better typed as a quality or a directedness, and whether the scope of field unraveling extends beyond moral fields.

proposal.utterance: A realist ontology of relation exists that makes obligation materially visible.

entities.label: RealistOntologyOfRelation
entities.rationale: A realist ontology of relation is a body of theoretical content — a pattern of propositions about the nature of relations — that can be instantiated in multiple physical bearers (texts, minds, inscriptions). It is therefore a generically dependent continuant, specifically an information artifact or theoretical framework.

entities.label: MaterialVisibility
entities.rationale: Material visibility is a quality of obligation — the property of being grounded in and perceptible through materially real relational structures. It inheres in an obligation-bearing entity and is made manifest by the relational ontology.

relations.rationale: Places the realist ontology of relation under the generically dependent continuant branch as an information content entity.
Material visibility is typed as a quality inhering in obligations.
Material visibility is a normative quality — it concerns how obligation becomes apparent within normative structures — so it is a sub-kind of the existing Normativity disposition class.

A realist ontology of relation is a constitutive theoretical framework for relational structures; placing it under RelationalConstitution (already a working class) captures the claim that it constitutes or articulates the relational ground of obligation.

open_questions: Is 'realist ontology of relation' intended as a specific named theoretical framework (an individual, e.g. the ontology described in a particular text), or a kind of ontological theory (a class)? Currently modeled as a class.

Does 'materially visible' mean obligation becomes empirically or perceptually accessible, or does it mean obligation has a material/physical grounding? This affects whether MaterialVisibility should be a Quality (BFO_0000019) or a Disposition (BFO_0000016).

proposal.utterance: Design in all its forms is a species of ethical expression.

entities.label: Design
entities.rationale: Design, in all its forms, is a purposive human activity that unfolds in time. As a kind of socially embedded, intentional process, it is best typed as a subclass of SocialProcess (itself a subclass of BFO Process). This captures the productive, temporal unfolding of designing.

entities.label: EthicalExpression
entities.rationale: Ethical expression is a normatively loaded disposition or capacity that is realized in processes bearing moral meaning. Typing it as a subclass of Normativity (itself a BFO Disposition) captures that it is an internally grounded tendency of agents and their acts to carry ethical significance. It could also be modeled as a quality, but the dispositional reading is stronger given the claim that design is a species of it.

relations.rationale: Design is a subkind of SocialProcess: it is a temporally extended, socially situated purposive activity.
EthicalExpression is a normative disposition, hence a subkind of Normativity.

The utterance asserts that design (in all its forms) is a species of ethical expression. This is encoded as Design being a subclass of EthicalExpression. Because EthicalExpression is a Disposition and Design is a Process, this cross-category subclass claim is ontologically problematic (see open_questions), but it is the most direct encoding of the assertion.

open_questions: The utterance equates a process kind (Design) with a dispositional kind (EthicalExpression), which creates a cross-category subsumption in BFO. One resolution: treat 'ethical expression' not as a class that Design is a subclass of, but as a role or quality that instances of Design bear — e.g., every Design process realizes an EthicalExpression disposition inhering in the designing agent. Should we model this as a universal restriction (every Design process realizes some EthicalExpression) rather than a subclass relation?

Is 'Design' intended to cover only intentional human design processes (graphic design, architecture, engineering), or also natural 'design-like' processes (evolutionary design, etc.)? This affects whether Person or Agent (or both) must participate.

Should EthicalExpression be modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in agents, or as a Quality (BFO_0000019) of the process/artifact? The dispositional reading seems stronger here, but the user may prefer otherwise.
Is MeaningBearing (already in the ontology, a subclass of Normativity) close enough to EthicalExpression that we should reuse or specialize it rather than mint a new class?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a genus-species relationship: Design is a species (subkind) of ethical expression. I mint two new classes: Design as a subclass of SocialProcess (BFO Process) capturing it as a temporally extended purposive human activity, and EthicalExpression as a subclass of Normativity (BFO Disposition) capturing the normative, meaning-laden character the utterance attributes to design. The subsumption relation Design rdfs:subClassOf EthicalExpression encodes the assertion directly, but flagged as problematic because it crosses BFO's process/disposition boundary. Alternative modellings (universal restriction via OWL, or a realized-in link) are raised in open questions. The existing class MeaningBearing is also flagged as a possible reuse candidate.

proposal.utterance: Environments we inhabit are never morally neutral.

entities.label: InhabitedEnvironment
entities.rationale: Environments we inhabit are places or sites in the BFO sense — spatially bounded regions in which agents are located and carry out activities. BFO_0000029 (Site) is the appropriate type for a bounded spatial context inhabited by agents.

entities.label: MoralValence
entities.rationale: Moral valence — the property of being morally charged (positive, negative, or non-neutral) — is a quality that inheres in an entity. It is a specifically dependent continuant of the Quality type, since it characterises the bearer and cannot exist independently.

entities.label: MoralNonNeutrality
entities.rationale: The utterance specifically asserts that inhabited environments are never morally neutral, i.e. they always bear a non-neutral moral valence. MoralNonNeutrality is a subclass of MoralValence, capturing this positive ontological commitment rather than merely the absence of a property.

relations.rationale: MoralValence is typed as a Quality (BFO_0000019), a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer.
MoralNonNeutrality is the specific species of MoralValence asserted by the utterance — all inhabited environments bear it.
InhabitedEnvironment is typed as a Site (BFO_0000029).

The utterance asserts that every inhabited environment bears (inheres in) some instance of MoralNonNeutrality. RO_0000052 (inheres in) captures that MoralNonNeutrality is a specifically dependent continuant whose bearer is an InhabitedEnvironment. In OWL this will be expressed as a universal restriction: MoralNonNeutrality SubClassOf inheres_in some InhabitedEnvironment.

open_questions: Should InhabitedEnvironment be placed under the existing working:IntersubjectiveWorld (BFO_0000029) or kept as a sibling Site class? The two notions overlap but IntersubjectiveWorld carries intersubjective/social connotations that 'environment' may not always require.
Is MoralValence better modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) — something that is realised in moral responses or judgements — rather than a Quality? The distinction matters for downstream reasoning.
Should MoralNonNeutrality be connected to working:MoralField or working:Normativity to link the environmental claim to the existing normative structure in the ontology?
Does 'environments we inhabit' include non-physical or virtual environments, or is it restricted to spatially bounded physical sites?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes a general ontological claim: every environment that agents inhabit bears a non-neutral moral character. This requires three new classes. First, InhabitedEnvironment (a Site, BFO_0000029) names the kind of spatial context at issue. Second, MoralValence (a Quality, BFO_0000019) is the generic property of having some moral charge; it inheres in material or immaterial entities. Third, MoralNonNeutrality is a subclass of MoralValence capturing the specific claim that the valence is never zero. The key assertion is modelled as a universal restriction: every InhabitedEnvironment bears some instance of MoralNonNeutrality (RO_0000052 / inheres_in). No individuals are minted because the claim is universal/generic. Open questions flag whether a Disposition type might be preferable to Quality, and whether these new classes should be linked to existing Normativity or MoralField structures already in the ontology.

proposal.utterance: Architecture and urban design are configurations of moral possibility.

entities.label: BuiltEnvironment
entities.rationale: Architecture and urban design produce built environments — material entities with mass and spatial extent (buildings, streets, public spaces). Modeled as a class of material entities.

entities.label: MoralPossibilityConfiguration
entities.rationale: A 'configuration of moral possibility' is a structured set of dispositions inhering in a material environment — it enables, constrains, or shapes what moral interactions, recognitions, and obligations can be realized therein. Subclass of RelationalConfiguration (itself a Disposition/BFO_0000016) and also tagged under Normativity context. This models the claim that built environments carry structurally embedded moral affordances.

entities.label: ArchitecturalDesignProcess
entities.rationale: Architecture and urban design are processes (social, intentional, material-transforming) through which built environments are produced and moral possibility configurations are realized. Subclass of SocialProcess.

relations.rationale: MoralPossibilityConfiguration is a species of RelationalConfiguration — it is a disposition structuring relational possibilities, here specifically moral ones.
A configuration of moral possibility is inherently normative — it determines what moral actions, encounters, and obligations are available or foreclosed.
Built environments bear moral possibility configurations as specifically dependent continuants inhering in them — the claim is that the material structure carries normative-dispositional structure.
The architectural design process realizes (or fails to realize) particular moral possibility configurations — the process instantiates the normative dispositions in the resulting built environment.
Built environments are material entities per BFO.
Architecture and urban design are social processes involving collective intentionality, norms, and material transformation.

open_questions: Should BuiltEnvironment also be typed as BFO_0000029 (Site), since buildings and urban spaces function as sites of social processes? Or should it remain purely BFO_0000040 (Material entity)? Some built environments function as sites while also being material.

Does 'moral possibility' here mean affordances for moral action (a disposition), or does it mean something closer to the moral field concept already in the ontology (MoralField)? Should MoralPossibilityConfiguration be modeled as a subclass of MoralField or kept distinct?

Should ArchitecturalDesignProcess carry an additional relation to MoralField (e.g., as constituting a moral field), given that the claim seems to assert that the built environment is itself a kind of moral topology?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a philosophically rich claim: that architecture and urban design are not merely physical artifacts or processes, but are normative structures — they configure what moral interactions, recognitions, obligations, and possibilities are available to the persons and agents who inhabit them. In BFO terms, this requires three new entities: (1) BuiltEnvironment as a class of material entities (the physical product of architectural design), (2) MoralPossibilityConfiguration as a class of dispositions (specifically dependent continuants) that inhere in built environments and constitute their normative structure — subclassed under the existing RelationalConfiguration and Normativity — and (3) ArchitecturalDesignProcess as a social process that produces built environments and realizes moral possibility configurations. The key ontological move is that moral possibility configurations are specifically dependent continuants borne by material entities (built environments), connecting physical structure to normative affordance. This preserves BFO's commitment to grounding normative structure in material bearers while capturing the claim's philosophical content. Open questions concern whether BuiltEnvironment should also be typed as Site, and whether MoralPossibilityConfiguration overlaps with the existing MoralField class.

proposal.utterance: The structure of space is morally charged because it mediates how beings become present to one another.

entities.label: SpatialStructure
entities.rationale: The 'structure of space' as a morally charged mediating feature is best typed as a disposition inhering in spatial/material arrangements—it is an internally grounded capacity to shape how beings become present to one another. It is not a quality (not a measurable magnitude) nor a role (not externally grounded by social position). Disposition captures an inherent tendency/power of spatial configurations.

entities.label: MoralCharge
entities.rationale: A 'moral charge' is a normatively loaded disposition that inheres in spatial or relational structures, grounding obligations or ethical salience. It is a sub-disposition of Normativity, representing the specific normative power spatial arrangements exercise.

entities.label: SpatialMediation
entities.rationale: The act by which spatial structure mediates how beings become present to one another is a process—a happening in time. It is a kind of DirectednessShapingRelation process, since it actively shapes the directedness of beings toward one another through spatial configuration.

entities.label: PresenceMediatedEncounter
entities.rationale: Beings 'becoming present to one another' through spatial mediation is a social process—an encounter constituted by how spatial structure shapes mutual presence. This extends SocialProcess to capture spatially mediated inter-being presence.

relations.rationale: MoralCharge is a specific normative disposition and thus a subclass of Normativity.
SpatialStructure is a disposition inhering in material/spatial arrangements.
SpatialMediation is a process that shapes relational directedness, making it a subclass of DirectednessShapingRelation.
PresenceMediatedEncounter is a social process in which beings become mutually present via spatial mediation.
The disposition SpatialStructure is realized in the process of SpatialMediation—the spatial structure's mediating capacity is exercised when spatial mediation occurs.
SpatialMediation is a constituent sub-process of PresenceMediatedEncounter, as the mediation is part of the encounter-event in which beings become present.

MoralCharge is the normatively specific form of SpatialStructure disposition—spatial structure is morally charged means it bears a MoralCharge disposition. MoralCharge subclasses SpatialStructure to capture that moral chargeability is a kind of spatial dispositional structure.

entities.label: SensoryDeprivationPrison

entities.rationale: The design of a prison for sensory deprivation is an internally grounded disposition inhering in the material structure of the prison: it is a capacity/tendency to produce sensory deprivation conditions in occupants. Modeled as a subclass of Disposition (BFO_0000016).

entities.label: RelationalPossibility
entities.rationale: Relational possibility is a disposition (a capacity to enter into or sustain relational configurations) inhering in a person or agent. It is a subclass of Relationality, which is already typed as BFO_0000016 in the ontology.

entities.label: SeveringOfRelationalPossibility
entities.rationale: The severing of relational possibility is a process — a happening in time — in which an agent's relational possibilities are destroyed or suppressed. It is a specific kind of process precipitated by the sensory deprivation environment.

entities.label: ErosionOfDirectedness
entities.rationale: The erosion of structures of directedness is a process in which dispositions of relational directedness (already in the ontology as RelationalDirectedness, BFO_0000016) are progressively degraded. Modeled as a process because it is a happening that unfolds through time.

The sensory deprivation design disposition inheres in the sensory deprivation prison (the material entity bearing this structural feature).
Relational possibility is a subtype of Relationality (capacity to enter relational configurations); Relationality is already BFO_0000016 in the working ontology.

The process of severing relational possibility realizes the sensory deprivation design disposition — the disposition is manifested/realized in this process when the prison operates on its inhabitants.

Erosion of structures of directedness is a more specific process that is part of or a subtype of the broader severing of relational possibility; directedness (RelationalDirectedness) is a subtype of Relationality, so eroding it is a specific kind of severing relational possibility.

Open for human review: if severing relational possibility is understood as a destructive or negating sub-process within or against the broader moral field realization process, a part-of relation to MoralFieldRealization captures that it is a moment within the unfolding of ethical life.

proposal.utterance: Institutions are field conditions for ethical presence, not neutral backgrounds to ethical action.

entities.label: Institution
entities.rationale: An institution in this ethical-social sense is a structured social site — a persistent, spatially and normatively bounded region within which agents participate. BFO Site (BFO_0000029) captures the idea of a place or context in which processes occur and roles are realized. IntersubjectiveWorld and MoralField already extend BFO_0000029; Institution is a sibling or sub-class that grounds ethical field conditions.

entities.label: FieldCondition
entities.rationale: A 'field condition' is an internally grounded capacity of an institution that structures the moral topology and makes ethical presence possible — not merely a background fact, but a normatively active disposition. Subclassing ObligationStructure (which already extends BFO_0000016) captures that it is a kind of structuring normative disposition.

entities.label: EthicalPresence
entities.rationale: Ethical presence is the normatively activated state of being a morally addressable, responsive agent within an institutional field — a realizable, internally grounded disposition that requires an institution as its realization milieu. Subclassing Normativity (itself under BFO_0000016) is appropriate.

relations.rationale: An institution is a kind of intersubjective world — a structured shared site — while being more determinate than the generic intersubjective world, so it is a subclass.
Field conditions are obligation-structuring dispositions; they belong under ObligationStructure to capture their normative generativity.
Ethical presence is a form of normativity — a realizable disposition toward moral responsiveness — so it subclasses Normativity.

Field conditions are constitutive features of moral fields; asserting FieldCondition as part of the MoralField structure makes explicit that institutions bear field conditions as aspects of the moral field they instantiate.
Ethical presence (a realizable) is realized in ethical life (a process), encoding that the activated ethical presence of agents unfolds through participation in ethical life.

open_questions: Should Institution be a subclass of IntersubjectiveWorld and/or MoralField, or a sibling? The utterance implies institutions are field conditions themselves — should we also model Institution as bearing a FieldCondition (i.e., Institution RO_0000053 FieldCondition) rather than being a subtype of site?

Is 'ethical presence' a disposition of persons (inhering in agents) or a relational property of the institution-agent encounter? This affects whether EthicalPresence is modeled as inhering in Person or in the Institution-Person interaction.

Should we distinguish 'background conditions' (the rejected view) ontologically — e.g., as a class NeutralBackground that is disjoint from FieldCondition — to formally capture the contrast the utterance asserts?

Is 'ObligationStructure' already defined as a parent in your ontology context? It appears as a parent of PreDiscursiveBinding and ObligationGeneratingCondition but is not listed as a working class itself — should it be minted explicitly?

The key philosophical move is replacing the passive-background model with an active-disposition model: institutions bear FieldConditions that structure the moral topology (linking to MoralField) and make EthicalPresence possible. This is consistent with the existing ontology's commitment to relational constitution, moral fields, and obligation-generating conditions.

proposal.utterance: Institutions are ethical to the extent that they recognize and support obligations arising from being-with.

entities.label: Institution
entities.rationale: Institutions are material entities (organizations, social bodies with physical presence and membership); they are independent continuants with mass and spatial extent (buildings, personnel, documents). They are not mere roles or dispositions—they are the bearers of roles and dispositions.

entities.label: InstitutionalEthicalQuality
entities.rationale: The degree to which an institution is ethical is a measurable quality inhering in the institution. It is a specifically dependent continuant (quality) because it cannot exist without the institution that bears it.

entities.label: BeingWith
entities.rationale: Being-with (Mitsein) is the existential-relational condition of co-presence with others, modeled as a disposition (internally grounded realizable) that inheres in agents. It grounds obligations and is a subtype of RelationalEmbeddedness already in the ontology.

entities.label: InstitutionalRecognitionDisposition
entities.rationale: The capacity of an institution to recognize obligations—i.e., its disposition to enact recognition processes toward agents—is an internally grounded realizable entity (disposition) inhering in the institution.

entities.label: InstitutionalSupportDisposition
entities.rationale: The capacity of an institution to actively support obligations arising from being-with—its disposition to sustain those obligations through practice—is a distinct disposition inhering in the institution.

entities.label: BeingWithObligation
entities.rationale: Obligations arising from being-with are a subtype of ObligationGeneratingCondition already in the ontology. They are realizable entities (dispositions) inhering in agents co-constituted through being-with relations.

relations.rationale: Institutions are a subtype of Agent in the working ontology—they are material entities capable of bearing roles and dispositions and participating in social processes.
InstitutionalEthicalQuality is a normative quality; it is typed under Normativity (itself a BFO_0000016) but re-typed as Quality (BFO_0000019). Open question flagged below about this tension.
The institutional disposition to recognize is a subtype of the Recognition class already in the ontology, restricting its realization to institutional bearers.
Supporting obligations is itself an obligation-generating condition that, when realized in institutional process, produces or sustains normative demands.

entities.rationale: Technologies are material entities — physical or artifact-based things with mass and spatial extent that persist through time. Typing as a class since 'technology' is a common noun denoting a kind.

entities.label: MoralSpaceMediation
entities.rationale: The mediating function of technology with respect to moral space is an internally grounded capacity — a disposition — that inheres in technologies and is realized in moral-field-involving processes. It is not a mere role (externally grounded) but a constitutive functional capacity. Typed under Normativity since it conditions the moral field.

entities.label: NeutralInstrumentDisposition
entities.rationale: The utterance explicitly negates that technologies bear a neutral-instrument disposition. Modeling this class allows the ontology to represent the denial (technologies are disjoint from bearers of NeutralInstrumentDisposition) and to contrast it with MoralSpaceMediation.

entities.label: TechnologicalMediation
entities.rationale: The actual mediating — technology shaping or conditioning the moral field in which agents interact — is a process, a happening unfolding in time. It is a species of MoralFieldRealization since it is precisely how the moral field is realized through technological involvement.

relations.rationale: MoralSpaceMediation is a normative disposition — a subclass of Normativity — because mediating moral space is itself a normative capacity affecting how obligations and moral relations are structured.
Technological mediation is a realization of the moral field through the involvement of technologies; it is therefore a subclass of MoralFieldRealization.
Establishes Technology as a material entity class.

The disposition MoralSpaceMediation inheres in (instances of) Technology — expressing that technologies bear this mediating capacity. Using RO_0000052 (inheres in) at the class level as a domain constraint.
The disposition MoralSpaceMediation is realized in instances of TechnologicalMediation processes.
Instances of TechnologicalMediation have Technology instances as participants — the technology is what does the mediating.
TechnologicalMediation also has the MoralField as a participant (the space being mediated), linking the process to the existing MoralField class.
Explicit assertion that Technology is a continuant (already implied via Material entity, but stated for reasoner clarity).

open_questions: Should 'Technology' be further restricted to artifact material entities (e.g., subclass of some Artifact class), given that natural objects are typically not called technologies? This would tighten the BFO typing.

The utterance negates the neutral-instrument view. Should we assert a formal disjointness axiom (Technology disjointWith bearer-of NeutralInstrumentDisposition) in the ontology, or is it sufficient to leave NeutralInstrumentDisposition as a foil class without an explicit disjointness?

Is 'moral space' here co-extensive with the existing working:MoralField (typed as BFO Site/IntersubjectiveWorld), or does it denote something broader or different — e.g., a topology of normative relations rather than a place-like site?
Should TechnologicalMediation be typed under working:SocialProcess rather than (or in addition to) working:MoralFieldRealization, given that technological mediation often occurs in social contexts?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes three claims: (1) technologies function as mediators of moral space, (2) this function is constitutive rather than neutral, and (3) the neutral-instrument framing is explicitly denied. To capture (1) I introduce Technology (a material entity class) and MoralSpaceMediation (a disposition inhering in technologies, subclassed under Normativity), realized in a new process class TechnologicalMediation (subclassed under the existing MoralFieldRealization). To capture (3) I introduce NeutralInstrumentDisposition as a foil class, which can later receive a disjointness axiom with MoralSpaceMediation once the user confirms. I reuse the existing MoralField individual class as the participant moral space in TechnologicalMediation. All new classes are BFO-typed: Technology as BFO_0000040, both disposition classes as BFO_0000016, and TechnologicalMediation as BFO_0000015.

entities.label: Continuity

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that four properties — Visibility, Intelligibility, Reciprocity, and Continuity — are ontological features of a kind called 'ethical relation.' In BFO terms, ontological features that are internally grounded and characterize how a kind of entity is disposed to behave or present itself are best modeled as dispositions (BFO_0000016). I first mint EthicalRelation as a class under Relationality and Normativity, since ethical relations are both structurally relational and normatively charged, consistent with the existing ontology's treatment. The four features are then minted as disposition subclasses, each placed under the most fitting existing working class: Visibility and Continuity under Relationality (general relational dispositions), Intelligibility under Normativity (with a link to existing MoralIntelligibility), and Reciprocity under RelationalConfiguration (structural mutual orientation). All four are also related to EthicalRelation via rdfs:subClassOf to capture their status as features of that kind. Several open questions are raised about whether the feature relationship should be expressed via property restrictions rather than class hierarchy, and whether some new classes overlap with existing ones.

proposal.utterance: Relational structure and ethical directedness are conditions for ethical life extended through technological mediation.

entities.label: TechnologicalMediation
entities.rationale: Technological mediation is a process by which technology intervenes in or extends social and ethical relations. It is a kind of SocialProcess (itself a subclass of BFO Process) in which material artifacts participate as mediating structures.

entities.label: TechnologicallyMediatedEthicalLife
entities.rationale: The utterance asserts that ethical life can be extended through technological mediation. This justifies a subclass of EthicalLife in which the realization involves technological mediation as a constitutive part-process.

entities.label: EthicalDirectedness
entities.rationale: The utterance distinguishes 'ethical directedness' as a condition for ethical life. It is a species of RelationalDirectedness (already in the ontology, a subclass of Disposition BFO_0000016), specifically oriented toward ethical obligations and moral fields.

relations.rationale: TechnologicallyMediatedEthicalLife is a specialization of EthicalLife, inheriting its normative and social-process character while adding technological mediation as a constitutive feature.
A technologically mediated ethical life has technological mediation as a part-process; BFO 'has part' (BFO_0000051) captures this mereological inclusion at the process level.

Reaffirming that relational structure (here captured by RelationalEmbeddedness, which is the closest existing class to 'relational structure') is a condition: the utterance says relational structure is a condition for ethical life, represented via the existing subClassOf chain from RelationalEmbeddedness through Relationality.
EthicalDirectedness is typed as a subclass of RelationalDirectedness, marking it as a disposition inhering in agents and oriented toward the ethical domain.
The disposition EthicalDirectedness is realized in processes of TechnologicallyMediatedEthicalLife, per the BFO 'realized in' relation (BFO_0000054).
The utterance asserts relational structure is a condition for ethical life; RelationalEmbeddedness as a disposition is realized in the process of TechnologicallyMediatedEthicalLife.

open_questions: Should 'relational structure' map specifically to RelationalEmbeddedness, or does the utterance intend a broader or different class (e.g., RelationalConfiguration or Relationality)?

Is TechnologicalMediation meant to be a process class (BFO Process) or a disposition/capacity of material artifacts (BFO Disposition)? Some accounts treat it as a capacity of artifacts that is realized in mediating processes.
Should 'ethical directedness' be distinguished from EthicalInterdependence (already in the ontology) or treated as a new, narrower subclass of RelationalDirectedness?

Does 'extended through technological mediation' imply that non-technologically-mediated EthicalLife also exists as a sibling class, or is all ethical life in scope potentially technologically mediated?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes three core ontological commitments: (1) relational structure is a condition for ethical life, (2) ethical directedness is a condition for ethical life, and (3) ethical life can be extended through technological mediation. For (1), RelationalEmbeddedness already exists as the closest proxy for 'relational structure' and is typed as a disposition (via RelationalConfiguration and Relationality subclassing BFO_0000016). For (2), EthicalDirectedness is minted as a new subclass of the existing RelationalDirectedness (BFO_0000016 Disposition), capturing the specifically ethical orientation of directedness. For (3), TechnologicalMediation is minted as a new subclass of SocialProcess, and TechnologicallyMediatedEthicalLife is minted as a subclass of EthicalLife having TechnologicalMediation as a part-process. Both conditions (RelationalEmbeddedness and EthicalDirectedness) are linked via 'realized in' to TechnologicallyMediatedEthicalLife, capturing their role as conditions for that extended form of ethical life.

proposal.utterance: Addressability requires visibility, linguistic access, identity persistence, and non-erasure.

entities.label: Addressability
entities.rationale: Addressability is the capacity of an agent or entity to be addressed — it is internally grounded in the entity and can be realized in communicative or recognition processes. Disposition (BFO_0000016) is the appropriate BFO type.

entities.label: Visibility
entities.rationale: Visibility is a property that inheres in an entity — the quality of being perceptible or recognizable within a social or moral field. Quality (BFO_0000019) is appropriate as it is a measurable/assessable property of the bearer.

entities.label: LinguisticAccess
entities.rationale: Linguistic access is the capacity to be engaged through language — to be named, addressed, or described linguistically. It is internally grounded in the bearer's linguistic constitution and realized in communicative processes. Disposition fits.

entities.label: IdentityPersistence
entities.rationale: Identity persistence is a property of an entity — the quality of maintaining a traceable identity over time. As a measurable, inhering property, Quality (BFO_0000019) is appropriate.

entities.label: NonErasure
entities.rationale: Non-erasure is the capacity of an agent not to be removed from the moral or social field — a normative disposition grounding continued addressability. Disposition (BFO_0000016) is appropriate as it is internally grounded and can be realized in protective social processes.

relations.rationale: Addressability is a kind of disposition inhering in agents or entities.
Visibility is a quality inhering in an entity.
LinguisticAccess is a disposition inhering in a being capable of linguistic engagement.
IdentityPersistence is a quality of maintaining traceable identity over time.
NonErasure is a disposition grounding the persistence of an entity within a moral or social field.

Addressability is closely related to MeaningBearer (already a Role in the ontology) in that it is a precondition for being meaningfully addressed; however, it is typed as Disposition rather than Role to capture its grounding character. This subClassOf relation is proposed cautiously — see open_questions.
Visibility is a component condition of Addressability — something must be visible to be addressable. Modeled as part-of at the class level (restriction).
LinguisticAccess is a required constituent of Addressability per the stated assertion.
IdentityPersistence is a required constituent of Addressability per the stated assertion.
NonErasure is a required constituent of Addressability per the stated assertion.

open_questions: Should Addressability be typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) or a Role (BFO_0000023)? If addressability is externally grounded in social recognition rather than internally grounded in the bearer, Role may be more appropriate.

The four conditions (Visibility, LinguisticAccess, IdentityPersistence, NonErasure) are stated as requirements of Addressability. Should these be modeled as necessary parts (part_of restrictions), as enabling conditions (related via some custom 'requires' property), or as sub-dispositions/qualities that must be co-present?

Should Visibility and IdentityPersistence be typed as Quality (BFO_0000019) or Disposition (BFO_0000016)? They could be either: as stable properties they are qualities; as capacities they are dispositions.

Is NonErasure a normative constraint (something like a right or obligation-structure) rather than a disposition? If so, it might be better typed under ObligationStructure or Normativity already in the ontology.
Should Addressability be linked to the existing working:MeaningBearer or working:RelationalDirectedness classes, given that being addressed is a form of relational directedness?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that Addressability — the capacity to be addressed — has four necessary conditions: Visibility, LinguisticAccess, IdentityPersistence, and NonErasure. I mint Addressability as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is internally grounded in the agent or entity and realized in communicative or recognition processes. Visibility and IdentityPersistence are typed as Qualities (BFO_0000019) because they are measurable, inhering properties of the bearer. LinguisticAccess and NonErasure are typed as Dispositions because they capture capacities (to engage linguistically, to resist erasure) that are internally grounded and realized in processes. The four conditions are related to Addressability via BFO part_of, modeling them as constituent elements of the complex disposition. I flag several open questions: whether Addressability is better a Role than a Disposition, whether the part_of modeling of conditions is correct or whether a custom 'requires' relation is needed, and whether NonErasure might fit better under existing Normativity or ObligationStructure classes already in the ontology.

entities.rationale: A professional decision is a temporally bounded happening — an act of deciding within a professional context — that unfolds in time. It is a kind of SocialProcess because it occurs within and is shaped by social structures, roles, and norms.

entities.label: VisibilitySelectivity
entities.rationale: The capacity of professional decisions to make certain relational directedness 'visible' is an internally grounded disposition inhering in the decision process or in the roles that shape it. It is a kind of RelationalDirectedness because it governs which relational orientations come into view.

entities.label: ActionabilitySelectivity
entities.rationale: The capacity to make relational directedness 'actionable' — i.e., to enable it to drive conduct — is a disposition that is a kind of NormativeForce, since it concerns which normative directions can be acted upon.

entities.label: BindingSelectivity
entities.rationale: The capacity to make relational directedness 'binding' is an obligation-generating disposition. It is a subtype of ObligationGeneratingCondition because it determines which relational relations generate binding obligations.

entities.label: RelationalVisibility
entities.rationale: The state of being 'visible' as a relational directedness — i.e., the quality of salience or perceptibility of a relational orientation within a professional context — is a quality inhering in the relational directedness itself.

relations.rationale: Professional decisions are a subkind of social process.
Visibility selectivity governs which relational directedness become salient, making it a species of relational directedness disposition.
Actionability selectivity determines which relational orientations can drive conduct, making it a species of normative force disposition.
Binding selectivity determines which relational directedness generates obligations, making it a species of obligation-generating condition.
A professional decision realizes visibility selectivity — through the decision, certain relational orientations become visible.
A professional decision realizes actionability selectivity — through the decision, certain relational orientations become actionable.
A professional decision realizes binding selectivity — through the decision, certain relational orientations become binding.
Relational visibility is a quality of relational directedness instances, specifying whether a given orientation is rendered perceptible or salient within a professional context.

open_questions: Should 'ProfessionalDecision' be a subclass of a more specific process class (e.g., a 'DecisionProcess' intermediate), or is direct subclassing under SocialProcess appropriate?

Is 'encoding' meant as a causal or constitutive relation between professional decisions and the selectivity dispositions? If constitutive, should we model ProfessionalDecision as constituting these dispositions rather than realizing them?

Are VisibilitySelectivity, ActionabilitySelectivity, and BindingSelectivity meant to inhere in the professional decision itself, in the role of the professional, or in the social institution that frames the decision?

Should 'RelationalVisibility' be a Quality (a static property) rather than a Disposition, or should it also be modeled as a Disposition since visibility can be actualized/deactualized through decisions?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that professional decisions function as selective encoders of relational directedness, determining which relational orientations become (a) visible, (b) actionable, and (c) binding. I model ProfessionalDecision as a subclass of SocialProcess (BFO Process), since deciding is a temporally unfolding happening. The three modes of encoding are modeled as dispositions (BFO Disposition): VisibilitySelectivity (subclass of RelationalDirectedness), ActionabilitySelectivity (subclass of NormativeForce), and BindingSelectivity (subclass of ObligationGeneratingCondition), because each is an internally grounded capacity of the decision process or the professional role. The relation between ProfessionalDecision and these dispositions is rendered via BFO's 'realizes' (BFO_0000055), though the open question of whether this is causal or constitutive warrants user clarification. RelationalVisibility is added as a Quality to capture the achieved state of being-made-visible for a relational directedness instance.

entities.label: InscribedNormativeStructure

As a pattern that can be copied and instantiated in different bearers, it fits BFO's Generically Dependent Continuant. We sub-type it under Normativity to capture its ethical-normative content.

entities.label: MaterialNormativeSubstrate
entities.rationale: Forms, screens, furniture, and similar physical artifacts are material entities that serve as substrates in which normative structures are inscribed. This class collects such material bearers of normative content.

entities.label: InstitutionalProtocol
entities.rationale: Protocols and schedules are generically dependent continuants — information objects specifying procedures — that can be instantiated across multiple material carriers. They are a species of InscribedNormativeStructure.

entities.label: LegalRegulation
entities.rationale: Zoning laws are legal regulations — generically dependent continuants encoding normative constraints — and are a species of InscribedNormativeStructure.

entities.label: ComputationalInterface
entities.rationale: APIs are computational interfaces — information structures specifying how interactions must proceed — and thus generically dependent continuants that can bear inscribed normative grammars. Subclass of InscribedNormativeStructure.

entities.label: NormativeInscription
entities.rationale: The act of 'inscribing' a grammar of ethical life into material or informational substrates is itself a process — a social/normative process by which ethical structures become embedded in artifacts. Sub-typed under EthicalLife as a species of that social process.

relations.rationale: Material substrates (forms, screens, furniture) ground normative structures materially; they are bearers of structural dependency relations that make ethical life possible.

Since inscription into screens, APIs, and designed artifacts is paradigmatically technologically mediated, NormativeInscription is also a subclass of TechnologicallyMediatedEthicalLife.
Protocols are a species of inscribed normative structure.
Zoning laws and analogous regulations are a species of inscribed normative structure.
APIs are a species of inscribed normative structure.

open_questions: Should 'forms' (as in paper/digital forms) and 'furniture' be distinguished as separate subclasses of MaterialNormativeSubstrate, or is one class sufficient?

The utterance uses 'grammar' metaphorically — clarification would help determine whether this is an information artifact or a structural disposition.

Should InscribedNormativeStructure be grounded under both BFO_0000031 (GDC) and working:Normativity (Disposition, BFO_0000016)? There is a potential type conflict since Normativity is typed under BFO_0000016 (Specifically Dependent Continuant) while GDC is BFO_0000031; these are disjoint in BFO. We should either make InscribedNormativeStructure a pure GDC with a separate normative quality relation, or keep it as a Disposition.

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts that the normative grammar structuring ethical life is not confined to minds or explicit rules but is distributed across and inscribed in heterogeneous material and informational substrates — physical artifacts (forms, screens, furniture), institutional structures (protocols, schedules, zoning laws), and computational infrastructure (APIs). Ontologically, this demands: (1) a class for the inscribed normative pattern itself, treated as a Generically Dependent Continuant because such grammars can be instantiated across multiple substrates; (2) a class for the material substrates that bear these inscriptions; (3) subclasses distinguishing protocol/schedule-type normative structures, legal regulations, and computational interfaces; and (4) a process class for the act of inscription through which ethical grammars become embedded in the world. proposal.utterance: All design either sustains or severs the conditions for ethical directedness.

entities.label: Design
entities.rationale: Design is a kind of process — a happening in which agents intentionally configure artifacts, systems, or environments. It unfolds in time and has participants, making BFO Process the appropriate type.

entities.label: EthicalDirectedness
entities.rationale: Ethical directedness is a disposition (internally grounded realizable) that agents bear toward others within a moral field — the capacity to be oriented toward and responsive to other agents as morally significant. It is a specific form of RelationalDirectedness already in the ontology.

entities.label: SustainingEthicalDirectedness
entities.rationale: A subkind of Design process in which the outcome preserves or strengthens the conditions under which ethical directedness can be realized. This models the 'sustains' arm of the disjunction.

entities.label: SeveringEthicalDirectedness
entities.rationale: A subkind of Design process in which the outcome disrupts or eliminates the conditions under which ethical directedness can be realized. This models the 'severs' arm of the disjunction.

entities.label: ConditionsForEthicalDirectedness
entities.rationale: The set of conditions (relational, material, social) whose presence is necessary for EthicalDirectedness to be realizable. As a disposition-enabling condition it fits under ObligationGeneratingCondition, which is already typed as a BFO Disposition subclass.

relations.rationale: EthicalDirectedness is a specific form of relational directedness oriented toward morally salient others.
These conditions, when present, generate or enable the obligation-structure within which ethical directedness can be realized.
Sustaining design is a proper subtype of Design.
Severing design is a proper subtype of Design.
Sustaining design is a species of the broader class of processes that shape directedness, already present in the ontology.
Severing design equally shapes (by negating) directedness, and so falls under DirectednessShapingRelation.
EthicalDirectedness as a realizable is realized in MoralFieldRealization processes — capturing that it becomes actual within those processes.

open_questions: Is 'Design' intended here in a narrow sense (intentional artifact design, UX/architecture) or a broader sense encompassing any intentional configuration of social or material conditions? This affects whether Design should be a subclass of SocialProcess or remain a direct subclass of BFO Process.

Should SustainingEthicalDirectedness and SeveringEthicalDirectedness be modeled as exhaustive and disjoint subclasses of Design (i.e., every Design instance is exactly one of them), or is there a third category of design that is neutral/indeterminate with respect to ethical directedness?

Is 'ConditionsForEthicalDirectedness' best treated as a disposition inhering in agents, a site/context (BFO Site), or a generically dependent pattern (information about what is required)? The current typing as Disposition/ObligationGeneratingCondition may need refinement.
Should Design instances always have an Agent as participant (via RO_0000057), or can non-agent systems count as design sources in your framework?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a normative-ontological claim: every instance of Design is either of a kind that sustains the conditions enabling ethical directedness or of a kind that severs them. This commits us to (1) a class Design as a BFO Process, (2) a class EthicalDirectedness as a realizable disposition inhering in agents and typed as a subclass of the existing RelationalDirectedness, (3) a class ConditionsForEthicalDirectedness as an ObligationGeneratingCondition capturing what must be in place for ethical directedness to be realizable, and (4) two process subclasses of Design — SustainingEthicalDirectedness and SeveringEthicalDirectedness — that relate to those conditions via the DirectednessShapingRelation class already in the ontology. The claim is universal ('all design'), which in OWL would be expressed as a covering axiom; the reasoner should validate consistency of the disjoint/exhaustive reading once the user confirms whether the partition is intended to be strict. No individuals are introduced because the utterance is a general claim about kinds, not about particular entities.

proposal.utterance: Relation is not optional; obligation arises wherever beings encounter each other across fields of addressability.

entities.label: FieldOfAddressability
entities.rationale: A 'field of addressability' is a bounded intersubjective space within which beings are mutually available to address and be addressed by one another. It is best modeled as a subclass of IntersubjectiveWorld (itself a Site/BFO_0000029), since it denotes a domain or region of possible encounter rather than a process or disposition.

entities.label: ObligationArisingFromEncounter
entities.rationale: The utterance asserts that obligation is not contingent but arises necessarily wherever beings encounter one another across fields of addressability. This necessity is best captured as a disposition (internally grounded realizable) that is triggered (realized) by inter-being encounter. It is a subclass of ObligationGeneratingCondition, which already exists as a parent of obligatory structures.

entities.label: NonOptionalRelationality
entities.rationale: The claim that 'relation is not optional' attributes a modal character to relationality itself — it is a quality of being-in-relation that makes the relational structure non-contingent or necessary. Modeling this as a Quality subclassing Relationality (which is already a BFO_0000016 Disposition) is a slight re-type; alternatively it could be a Disposition. Flagged in open_questions.

entities.label: InterBeingEncounter
entities.rationale: Encounter between beings across fields of addressability is an occurrent process. It is a subclass of SocialProcess. When realized, it triggers the ObligationArisingFromEncounter disposition. This is distinct from but related to Recognition (already in the ontology), which is one possible outcome of such an encounter.

relations.rationale: A field of addressability is a specific kind of intersubjective world/site within which beings are mutually available to one another.
Obligation arising from encounter is a species of obligation-generating condition, triggered whenever beings meet across addressable fields.
Non-optional relationality is a specific character of relationality asserting its non-contingent, necessary nature.
An inter-being encounter is a social process in which two or more beings come into mutual presence within a field of addressability.
The disposition to generate obligation is realized in (triggered by) the process of inter-being encounter, per the utterance's claim that obligation arises wherever beings encounter each other.
An inter-being encounter occurs within (is part of) a field of addressability — the site that makes mutual address possible.

open_questions: NonOptionalRelationality is proposed as a Quality (BFO_0000019) of the relational structure, but it could alternatively be a Disposition (BFO_0000016) since it grounds a necessary tendency. Which typing better fits your theoretical intent?

Should InterBeingEncounter be kept distinct from Recognition (already in the ontology), or is every inter-being encounter in this sense already a Recognition event? If they partially overlap, should Recognition be made a subclass of InterBeingEncounter?

The utterance speaks of 'beings' broadly — should this ontology treat 'being' as coextensive with Agent, or is there a need for a broader class (e.g., Sentient or Moral Patient) that includes non-agent entities capable of encounter?

proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance makes two tightly linked philosophical claims: (1) relationality is non-optional — wherever beings exist, they are always already in relation; and (2) obligation arises necessarily at the point of encounter, not by choice or consent. Open questions flag potential mergers with existing classes (MoralField, Recognition) and the typing of NonOptionalRelationality.

proposal.utterance: Democratic legitimacy fails when responsiveness to being-with is absent, not merely when turnout is low.

entities.label: DemocraticLegitimacy
entities.rationale: Democratic legitimacy is an internally grounded normative capacity or standing of a political system — it is a disposition (BFO_0000016) that a political institution bears, grounded in its relational properties. It is a species of Normativity already in the ontology.

entities.label: DemocraticLegitimacyFailure
entities.rationale: The failure of democratic legitimacy is an occurrent — a process or processual state — in which the normative capacity for legitimate governance is not realized. Typed as a SocialProcess (subclass of BFO_0000015).

entities.label: ResponsivenessToBeingWith
entities.rationale: Responsiveness to being-with is a disposition of a political or social agent to orient toward and acknowledge the relational co-presence (being-with, Mitsein) of those governed. It is a RelationalDirectedness disposition (BFO_0000016), capturing the directed, outward-facing relational character of the concept.

entities.label: BeingWith
entities.rationale: Being-with (Mitsein, Heidegger/Butler) is a fundamental relational mode of human existence — the ontological condition of co-presence with others. As a relational embeddedness condition it is a disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in agents situated with others. Subclassed under RelationalEmbeddedness.

entities.label: ElectoralTurnout
entities.rationale: Electoral turnout is a measurable quality of an electoral process — a proportion or rate. As a quality (BFO_0000019) it inheres in an electoral event or population. It is introduced as a contrast class: the utterance asserts that low turnout alone is insufficient to constitute legitimacy failure.

entities.label: AbsenceOfResponsivenessCondition
entities.rationale: The absence of responsiveness to being-with is identified as the condition that generates or constitutes democratic legitimacy failure. This is a negatively realized ObligationGeneratingCondition — a disposition whose non-realization triggers normative breakdown. Subclassed under ObligationGeneratingCondition (which is already in the ontology as a BFO_0000016 subclass).

relations.rationale: Democratic legitimacy is a species of normative standing, a subclass of Normativity.
The failure of democratic legitimacy is a social process — an occurrent unfolding in a political community.
Responsiveness to being-with is a form of relational directedness, orienting toward others in co-presence.
Being-with is a fundamental mode of relational embeddedness, the ontological co-situatedness of agents.
Responsiveness to being-with presupposes and is directed toward the condition of being-with; it is a more specific relational disposition within that broader existential condition.

The absence of responsiveness to being-with functions as the condition that generates (triggers) democratic legitimacy failure — it is an ObligationGeneratingCondition whose non-fulfillment is normatively decisive.
The failure process realizes (in the sense of making manifest) the absence-of-responsiveness condition. BFO_0000055 (realizes) links the process to the realizable it actualizes.
Democratic legitimacy as a normative disposition is realized in (BFO_0000054) processes of responsiveness to being-with — when such responsiveness occurs, legitimacy is actualized.

Is 'DemocraticLegitimacy' a disposition of a political institution (Material Entity bearer) or of a social process? If the former, should we introduce a class for 'PoliticalInstitution' as a Material Entity?

Should 'AbsenceOfResponsivenessCondition' be modeled as a privation/absence (which BFO does not natively support) rather than a positive disposition? If so, how would you like to represent the absence formally?

entities.label: UnprotectedRole

entities.label: MoralCountability
entities.rationale: The disposition to count—to be recognized as a morally considerable entity whose life and needs register in social and political deliberation. Crisis actualizes or reveals whether this disposition is realized.

proposal.utterance: Liberal democracy institutionalizes mutual addressability.

entities.label: LiberalDemocracy
entities.rationale: Liberal democracy is a form of political organization — a complex, institutionalized disposition of social bodies to structure governance around rights and mutual accountability. It could also be typed as a Site or as a GDC (the normative content of a constitutional order). Here we tentatively type it as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because 'liberal democracy' names the institutionalized capacity/disposition of a polity to enact certain processes. Open to revision.

entities.label: InstitutionalizationOfMutualAddressability
entities.rationale: Institutionalization is a social process by which norms or capacities (here, mutual addressability) become embedded in stable social structures. It is an occurrent — a process — that realizes the disposition of liberal democracy and whose output is a standing normative arrangement.

entities.label: MutualAddressability
entities.rationale: Mutual addressability is the capacity of agents within a normative order to address and be addressed by one another as morally significant persons. It is internally grounded in the normative structure of the community and is thus a Disposition (BFO_0000016) under the existing Normativity class. It relates closely to the existing OntologicalNecessityOfAddressability and AddressedByOther classes, but 'mutual addressability' names the symmetric, jointly-held disposition rather than a unidirectional or necessity claim.

relations.rationale: The disposition of liberal democracy is realized in the process of institutionalizing mutual addressability — BFO realized-in (BFO_0000054) links a realizable entity to the process in which it is realized.
The institutionalization process realizes the disposition of mutual addressability — BFO realizes (BFO_0000055) links the process to the realizable it brings about.
Mutual addressability is a specific, symmetrized form of the more general OntologicalNecessityOfAddressability already in the ontology; subclassing captures this relation.

Mutual addressability entails and refines the AddressedByOther disposition (being open to address from others), so it subclasses it. The 'mutual' qualifier adds the symmetric, co-constituted character.

open_questions: Should 'LiberalDemocracy' be typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) inhering in a Polity/State material entity, or as a Generically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000031) representing the normative/constitutional content of the democratic order? The GDC typing would be appropriate if we mean the normative text or abstract system of rules; the Disposition typing fits if we mean the standing capacity of a political community.
Should there be an individual 'liberal-democratic polity' (as a Material Entity/Site) that bears the LiberalDemocracy disposition, or is this utterance purely a claim about the class relationship?

Is 'institutionalizes' meant to assert a generic/class-level relationship (all instances of liberal democracy realize mutual addressability) or a particular historical claim? The current proposal models it generically.
Should MutualAddressability be further decomposed into 'AddressAbility' (active) and 'AddressedByOther' (passive) symmetric pair, or kept as a unified class?

Three new classes are proposed: LiberalDemocracy (tentatively a Disposition of a polity, BFO_0000016), InstitutionalizationOfMutualAddressability (a SocialProcess, BFO_0000015), and MutualAddressability (a Disposition under the existing Normativity branch). The realized-in / realizes BFO relations link the disposition of liberal democracy to the institutionalization process and then to the mutual addressability disposition it brings about. MutualAddressability is also subclassed under the existing OntologicalNecessityOfAddressability and AddressedByOther classes to anchor it in the existing ontology. The main open question concerns the correct BFO typing of 'liberal democracy' itself, which could be a Disposition inhering in a material political community or a Generically Dependent Continuant (a normative system whose content can be instantiated in many constitutions).

entities.rationale: Co-presence is a relational quality inhering in a plurality of agents or persons who share spatiotemporal situatedness. Typed as BFO Quality (BFO_0000019).

Disenfranchisement typically operates across political, civic, and social domains simultaneously, making it a species of MultiDomainSubjection — the condition of being subjected across multiple relational domains.

proposal.utterance: The good is fidelity to being, enacted in faithful attunement to what relation discloses.

entities.label: FidelityToBeing
entities.rationale: Fidelity to being is an internally grounded normative orientation — a disposition of an agent toward being as such. It fits under Normativity (itself a subclass of BFO Disposition) since it shapes how an agent is directed toward what is normatively significant.

entities.label: FaithfulAttunement
entities.rationale: Faithful attunement is an orientational disposition toward what relation discloses — it is directedness shaped by relational disclosure. It fits under RelationalDirectedness since it describes the quality of being appropriately oriented toward relationally disclosed content.

entities.label: RelationalDisclosure
entities.rationale: Relational disclosure is the process by which relation makes something manifest or available — what relation 'discloses' is a process-result structure. It fits under DirectednessShapingRelation as a process that shapes how agents are directed by revealing content through relational engagement.

entities.label: EnactmentOfGood
entities.rationale: The utterance states that the good is enacted — this is a moral realization process. EnactmentOfGood is the process in which fidelity to being is realized, fitting as a subclass of MoralFieldRealization (which is already a subclass of BFO Process).

relations.rationale: The utterance says 'the good is fidelity to being, enacted' — fidelity to being is realized in the enactment process. BFO realized_in links a disposition to the process in which it is realized.
Faithful attunement is described as the specific mode by which fidelity to being is enacted — it is the form fidelity takes in relational context, making it a subclass of FidelityToBeing.
The enactment process realizes faithful attunement — it is the occurrence in which FaithfulAttunement (as disposition) is expressed.
Faithful attunement is attuned to what relation discloses — it is realized in or oriented toward RelationalDisclosure as process.

open_questions: Is 'fidelity to being' best typed as a Disposition (internally grounded) or as a Role or Quality? The utterance suggests it is a normative orientation that can be enacted, which favors Disposition, but it might also be read as a Quality of an agent's existential stance.

Should 'the good' itself be introduced as a class (e.g., working:TheGood) identified with FidelityToBeing, or is the utterance asserting a definitional equivalence (owl:equivalentClass) between TheGood and FidelityToBeing?

Is 'relational disclosure' best modeled as a Process (something that happens) or as a Generically Dependent Continuant (information/content that is disclosed)? The utterance says 'what relation discloses' which could be the content (GDC) or the disclosing event (Process).
Does 'enacted in faithful attunement' imply that an Agent participant is presupposed, and should we add a participation relation from Agent to EnactmentOfGood?
proposal.rationale_summary: The utterance asserts a normative-ontological claim: the good is identified with fidelity to being, and this fidelity is enacted through faithful attunement to what relational processes disclose. Four new classes are proposed: FidelityToBeing (a Disposition under Normativity, capturing the normative orientation toward being), FaithfulAttunement (a Disposition under RelationalDirectedness, capturing the responsive orientation toward relational disclosure), RelationalDisclosure (a Process under DirectednessShapingRelation, capturing the disclosive character of relation), and EnactmentOfGood (a Process under MoralFieldRealization, capturing the occurrence in which fidelity is made real). Relations link fidelity to its enactment via BFO realized_in, and faithful attunement is nested under fidelity as its relational form. No individuals are asserted. Several open questions remain about whether 'the good' should be a named class, whether disclosure is a process or content, and whether an agent participant should be made explicit.
